## File: README.md

# @mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit

Reusable PgBouncer setup for the MGPL Diagnostics services. PgBouncer sits between the services and
PostgreSQL and shares a small number of server connections among many clients, so the api can run
several instances (and its worker) without exhausting PostgreSQL's `max_connections`.

The kit writes PgBouncer's two files and helps you run and watch it:

- **`pgbouncer.ini`** from typed configuration or `PGBOUNCER_*` environment variables, checked
  before it is written (`renderIni`, `configFromEnv`);
- **`userlist.txt`** with SCRAM-SHA-256 verifiers (or MD5), never plain passwords unless you ask
  (`renderUserlist`, `scramVerifier`), plus the SQL that puts the same verifier on PostgreSQL
  (`alterRoleSql`) and a safe `auth_query` setup (`authQuerySetupSql`);
- a **docker-compose service** with a health check (`renderCompose`);
- **TLS** on both sides (apps → PgBouncer, PgBouncer → PostgreSQL);
- a **readiness probe** that needs no credentials (`probePgBouncer`, `waitForPgBouncer`, `readiness`);
- a **CLI**, `mgpl-pgbouncer`, for container entrypoints and one-off setup.

It is a library with **no runtime dependencies** and no framework: use it from a script, a
container entrypoint or a service's start-up code. It does not run PgBouncer itself.

## Where it is used

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph services["MGPL services (PostgreSQL backend)"]
    api["api: GraphQL server<br/>(one or more instances)"]
    worker["api: worker<br/>(BullMQ jobs)"]
    other["any other service<br/>using db-kit's pg backend"]
  end
  pgb["PgBouncer<br/>(configured by pgbouncer-kit)"]
  pg[("PostgreSQL")]
  api --> pgb
  worker --> pgb
  other --> pgb
  pgb --> pg
  migrate["migrations, seed, pg_dump"] -. "direct, not through PgBouncer" .-> pg
```

| Consumer | How it reaches PostgreSQL today | With pgbouncer-kit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [api](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/api) server (`src/main.ts`) | `DATABASE_URL` → db-kit `createDb` (Sequelize) | `DATABASE_URL` points at PgBouncer (`pgbouncerUrl`); `GET /health` can include `readiness()` |
| api worker (`src/worker.ts`) | the same container and `DATABASE_URL` | the same PgBouncer, so jobs share the server pool with requests |
| finance-kit, ledger-kit | run inside the api process on db-kit's `Repositories` | nothing to change: they use the api's connection |
| [db-kit](https://github.com/mgpl-diagnostics/db-kit) PostgreSQL backend | `createDb({ url })` | nothing to change: it is transaction-safe (no session `SET`, advisory locks or `LISTEN`) |
| Migrations, `npm run seed`, backups | `DATABASE_URL` | keep a **direct** URL (`DIRECT_DATABASE_URL` or similar): DDL and dumps should not go through transaction pooling |

The MongoDB backend and Redis are not affected. The api will adopt this kit in a later step; until
then, the api's own PgBouncer settings stay where they are.

## Install

```bash
# .npmrc: @mgpl-diagnostics:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
npm install @mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit
```

Needs Node.js ≥ 20 and PgBouncer **≥ 1.21** (for `max_prepared_statements`; the compose image is 1.25).

## Adopting it in a service

Four steps; the example is the api with docker compose.

**1. Give PostgreSQL and PgBouncer the same SCRAM verifier.** PgBouncer can pass a client's SCRAM
login through to PostgreSQL only when both hold the same verifier. Make one, set it on PostgreSQL,
keep it for PgBouncer:

```bash
printf '%s' "$APP_DB_PASSWORD" | npx mgpl-pgbouncer verifier app
# SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:…        ← goes into PGBOUNCER_USERS (a verifier, not the password)
# ALTER ROLE "app" PASSWORD 'SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:…';   ← run once on PostgreSQL
```

(Alternatives: read the existing verifiers with `PG_SHADOW_QUERY` + `userlistFromRows`, or use
`auth_query`, below.)

**2. Render the files** in the container entrypoint or a deploy step:

```bash
PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL='postgres://db.internal:5432/mgpl?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/etc/pgbouncer/tls/ca.crt' \
PGBOUNCER_USERS="app:$APP_SCRAM_VERIFIER" \
sudo -E npx mgpl-pgbouncer render --out ./pgbouncer --chown 70
# wrote ./pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini and ./pgbouncer/userlist.txt (1 users)
```

`userlist.txt` is written with mode 600; the compose image runs as `postgres` (uid 70), so it must
own the file (`--chown 70`, which needs root, or `chown 70:70` afterwards).

**3. Add the compose service** and point the services at it:

```bash
npx mgpl-pgbouncer compose --tls-dir ./tls > compose.pgbouncer.yml
docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.pgbouncer.yml up -d
```

```yaml
# compose.yml (the api's services)
services:
  api:
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:${APP_DB_PASSWORD}@pgbouncer:6432/mgpl
    depends_on:
      pgbouncer: { condition: service_healthy }
  worker:
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:${APP_DB_PASSWORD}@pgbouncer:6432/mgpl
```

Or derive the URL in code: `pgbouncerUrl(process.env.DATABASE_URL, { host: "pgbouncer" })`.

**4. Size the app's own pool and add readiness.** Each app instance keeps its Sequelize pool
(`pool.max`, default 5); PgBouncer multiplexes all of them onto `default_pool_size` server
connections per user and database. Keep `instances × pool.max` ≤ `max_client_conn`, and
`default_pool_size + reserve_pool_size` below PostgreSQL's `max_connections` minus what admin tools need.

```ts
import { readiness, waitForPgBouncer } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit";

await waitForPgBouncer({ host: "pgbouncer", port: 6432 });            // at start-up
const ready = readiness({ host: "pgbouncer", port: 6432, query: () => db.sequelize.query("SELECT 1") });
// in GET /health: const r = await ready(); reply.code(r.ok ? 200 : 503).send(r);
```

Things that break under transaction pooling, and must not be used through PgBouncer: `SET` outside
a transaction (use `SET LOCAL`), session advisory locks (`pg_advisory_xact_lock` is fine), `LISTEN`,
`WITH HOLD` cursors, temporary tables that outlive a transaction. db-kit uses none of them.

## Configuration in code

```ts
import { defineConfig, renderIni, renderUserlist } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit";

const config = defineConfig({
  databases: [{ name: "mgpl", host: "db.internal", port: 5432 }],
  defaultPoolSize: 25,
  serverTls: { mode: "verify-full", caFile: "/etc/pgbouncer/tls/ca.crt" },
  statsUsers: ["metrics"],
});
await writeFile("pgbouncer.ini", renderIni(config));
await writeFile("userlist.txt", renderUserlist([{ user: "app", secret: verifier }]), { mode: 0o600 });
```

`defineConfig` checks everything and throws `PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG` with **every** problem listed in
`error.problems`. Values cannot inject lines or settings; database entries cannot carry passwords;
`trust` and `any` auth are refused.

### Defaults, and why

| Setting | Default | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pool_mode` | `transaction` | the point of PgBouncer for a stateless API; db-kit is transaction-safe |
| `listen_addr` / `listen_port` | `0.0.0.0` / `6432` | a container on a private network; PgBouncer's usual port |
| `auth_type` | `scram-sha-256` | PostgreSQL's default since 14; MD5 is legacy |
| `max_client_conn` | 500 | many app instances × their pools |
| `default_pool_size` | 20 | server connections per user + database |
| `min_pool_size` | 0 | no idle connections held open |
| `reserve_pool_size` / `reserve_pool_timeout` | 5 / 3 s | a little headroom for bursts |
| `max_db_connections` | 0 (no cap) | PgBouncer's default; set it when several users share one database |
| `max_prepared_statements` | 200 | named prepared statements work in transaction mode (PgBouncer ≥ 1.21) |
| `server_lifetime` / `server_idle_timeout` | 3600 s / 600 s | PgBouncer's defaults |
| `query_wait_timeout` | 120 s | PgBouncer's default |
| `ignore_startup_parameters` | `extra_float_digits` | sent by some drivers; harmless |
| `client_tls_sslmode` | `disable` | apps reach PgBouncer over the private compose network |
| `server_tls_sslmode` | `prefer`, or the upstream URL's `sslmode` | use `verify-full` with managed PostgreSQL |
| `log_connections` / `log_disconnections` | off | busy pools are noisy; pooler errors stay on |
| admin / stats users | none | add them explicitly |

### Environment variables

`configFromEnv(env)` and `usersFromEnv(env)` read these (also exported as `ENV_VARS`). Bad values
throw `PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV` listing every problem.

| Variable | Sets |
| --- | --- |
| `PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL` | PostgreSQL URL PgBouncer forwards to (host, port, database; user and password go to the userlist) |
| `PGBOUNCER_DATABASES` | more upstreams, comma-separated `[name=]postgres://…` |
| `PGBOUNCER_USERS` | extra users, comma-separated `user:secret` (SCRAM verifier, md5 secret, or a percent-encoded password) |
| `PGBOUNCER_USER_SECRET` | how plain passwords are stored: `scram` (default), `md5`, `plain` |
| `PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_ADDR`, `PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_PORT` | `listen_addr`, `listen_port` |
| `PGBOUNCER_POOL_MODE` | `pool_mode` |
| `PGBOUNCER_MAX_CLIENT_CONN`, `PGBOUNCER_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE`, `PGBOUNCER_MIN_POOL_SIZE` | pool sizes |
| `PGBOUNCER_RESERVE_POOL_SIZE`, `PGBOUNCER_RESERVE_POOL_TIMEOUT`, `PGBOUNCER_MAX_DB_CONNECTIONS` | reserve and caps |
| `PGBOUNCER_MAX_PREPARED_STATEMENTS` | `max_prepared_statements` |
| `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_LIFETIME`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | server connection timing (seconds) |
| `PGBOUNCER_QUERY_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `PGBOUNCER_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT` | client timing (seconds) |
| `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_TYPE`, `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_HBA_FILE` | `auth_type`, `auth_file`, `auth_hba_file` |
| `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_QUERY`, `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_USER`, `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_DBNAME` | `auth_query`, `auth_user`, `auth_dbname` |
| `PGBOUNCER_AUTH_PASSWORD` | password of the auth user, written in plain text (PgBouncer logs in as it) |
| `PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_USERS`, `PGBOUNCER_STATS_USERS` | console users, comma-separated |
| `PGBOUNCER_IGNORE_STARTUP_PARAMETERS` | comma-separated |
| `PGBOUNCER_LOG_CONNECTIONS` | `true` / `false` |
| `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_SSLMODE`, `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_CERT_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_KEY_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_CA_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_PROTOCOLS`, `PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_CIPHERS` | apps → PgBouncer TLS |
| `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_SSLMODE`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_CERT_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_KEY_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_CA_FILE`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_PROTOCOLS`, `PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_CIPHERS` | PgBouncer → PostgreSQL TLS (defaults from the upstream URL's `sslmode` and `sslrootcert`) |

The upstream URL's password is only used for the userlist, never written to `pgbouncer.ini`.

## Users and authentication

PgBouncer checks each client against `userlist.txt` and then logs in to PostgreSQL as the same user.
With SCRAM it can only do the second step when its verifier **equals** PostgreSQL's. Three ways:

1. **Same verifier on both sides** (recommended): `scramVerifier(password)` once, `alterRoleSql(user, verifier)`
   on PostgreSQL, the verifier in `PGBOUNCER_USERS`. The password never reaches PgBouncer's files.
2. **Copy PostgreSQL's verifiers**: run `PG_SHADOW_QUERY` as a superuser, `userlistFromRows(rows)`.
3. **`auth_query`**: PgBouncer looks users up in PostgreSQL. Run `authQuerySetupSql("pgbouncer_auth")`
   once (it creates a role and a `SECURITY DEFINER` lookup that never returns superusers), set
   `auth.query: AUTH_QUERY`, `auth.user: "pgbouncer_auth"`, and put that user in the userlist with
   `format: "plain"` (`PGBOUNCER_AUTH_PASSWORD`): PgBouncer logs in as it itself.

A plain password in `renderUserlist` becomes a SCRAM verifier with a random salt, which works for
client logins but not for SCRAM pass-through unless PostgreSQL gets the same verifier (way 1).
`saslprep` normalises passwords exactly as PostgreSQL does; `npm test` checks verifiers against
PostgreSQL for ASCII and Unicode passwords.

## TLS

```ts
defineConfig({
  databases: [...],
  clientTls: { mode: "require", certFile: "/etc/pgbouncer/tls/server.crt", keyFile: "/etc/pgbouncer/tls/server.key" },
  serverTls: { mode: "verify-full", caFile: "/etc/pgbouncer/tls/ca.crt", protocols: "secure" },
});
```

Client TLS needs a certificate and key; `verify-ca` / `verify-full` need a CA file; `auth.type: "cert"`
needs client TLS. Mount the files with `renderCompose({ tlsDir: "./tls" })` (read-only at `/etc/pgbouncer/tls`).

## Health

- `probePgBouncer({ host, port, timeoutMs })` opens a TCP connection, sends PostgreSQL's SSLRequest and
  reads the one-byte answer: up, speaking the protocol, and whether it offers TLS. No credentials, no pool slot.
- `waitForPgBouncer({ ..., waitMs, intervalMs })` retries until it answers, else `PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE`.
- `readiness({ ..., query })` returns a function for a health endpoint; `query` is an optional
  end-to-end check with your own driver. Errors are summarised (first line, 200 characters), never thrown.

The compose service uses `pg_isready` from the image for its own health check.

## CLI

```text
mgpl-pgbouncer render [--out DIR] [--chown UID[:GID]]
                                        pgbouncer.ini + userlist.txt (mode 600) from PGBOUNCER_* variables
mgpl-pgbouncer verifier USER            password on stdin → SCRAM verifier + ALTER ROLE statement
mgpl-pgbouncer auth-setup [AUTH_USER]   SQL for auth_query
mgpl-pgbouncer compose [--name N] [--port P] [--config-dir D] [--tls-dir D] [--publish [IP:]PORT] [--image I] [--depends-on a,b]
mgpl-pgbouncer check [--host H] [--port P] [--wait MS]
```

It prints paths and verifiers, never a password.

## Errors

`PgBouncerError.code` is a public contract (add, never rename); `error.problems` lists every problem.

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG` | `defineConfig` / `renderIni` / compose options are invalid |
| `PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV` | a `PGBOUNCER_*` variable is invalid or missing |
| `PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL` | not a `postgres://` URL |
| `PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER` | bad user name, empty or multi-line password, malformed verifier, duplicate user |
| `PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE` | `waitForPgBouncer` gave up |

## Develop

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run llms   # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI fails when it is stale)
```

`npm test` runs the unit checks and, when PostgreSQL (`PG_BIN`, default the newest
`/usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin`) and PgBouncer (`PGBOUNCER_BIN`, default on `PATH`) are installed, a real
PostgreSQL and real PgBouncers: SCRAM pass-through with the kit's verifiers, `auth_query`, transaction
pooling with prepared statements, the admin console, and the CLI's files. CI installs both and sets
`REQUIRE_PGBOUNCER=1`, so nothing is skipped there.

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit

Reusable PgBouncer setup for the MGPL Diagnostics services: env-driven `pgbouncer.ini`, SCRAM/MD5
userlists, `auth_query` SQL, a docker-compose service, TLS options, a readiness probe and the
`mgpl-pgbouncer` CLI. **A library: no server, no GraphQL, no runtime dependencies. It does not run
PgBouncer.** Consumers: the api server and worker (and any service on db-kit's PostgreSQL backend);
see the README's "Where it is used".

## Map

```
src/errors.ts     PgBouncerError (codes + problems), isPgBouncerError
src/config.ts     PgBouncerConfig, DEFAULT_CONFIG, defineConfig (fills defaults, lists every problem)
src/ini.ts        renderIni → pgbouncer.ini (no passwords)
src/env.ts        ENV_VARS, configFromEnv, usersFromEnv, secretFormatFromEnv
src/userlist.ts   saslprep, scramVerifier, verifyScram, md5Secret, renderUserlist/parseUserlist,
                  userlistFromRows + PG_SHADOW_QUERY, alterRoleSql, authQuerySetupSql + AUTH_QUERY
src/url.ts        parsePostgresUrl, pgbouncerUrl (rewrite DATABASE_URL to go through PgBouncer)
src/compose.ts    DEFAULT_IMAGE, composeService, renderCompose (YAML)
src/health.ts     probePgBouncer (SSLRequest), waitForPgBouncer, readiness
src/cli.ts        mgpl-pgbouncer: render, verifier, auth-setup, compose, check
scripts/test.ts   unit checks + real PostgreSQL and PgBouncer (SCRAM pass-through, auth_query, CLI files)
```

## Rules

1. **No passwords in pgbouncer.ini.** Database entries never carry one (`defineConfig` refuses it);
   passwords and verifiers live only in the userlist, written with mode 600.
2. **SCRAM by default.** Plain passwords become verifiers unless the caller asks for `plain` (the
   `auth_query` user is the one case that needs it). `scramVerifier` must equal PostgreSQL's for the
   same salt; the integration test checks ASCII and Unicode passwords against a real server.
3. **Every written value is checked.** No control characters, no line breaks, no `=`/quotes/spaces in
   names, no setting set twice (`extra` cannot repeat a key the kit owns). `trust`/`any` auth are refused.
4. **Errors list every problem** (`error.problems`). Codes (`PgBouncerError.code`) are a public
   contract: add, never rename.
5. **The probe uses no credentials** and holds no pool slot. Health output never contains a password.
6. Every new environment variable goes in `ENV_VARS` **and** the README table (a test checks both).
7. Defaults are documented in the README's "Defaults, and why"; change both together.
8. Zero runtime dependencies; Node.js built-ins only. `pg` is a dev dependency for the tests.
9. The kit does not edit consumers. The api adopts it in its own PR.
10. Never commit secrets, `.env` files, certificates or patient data. Tests use throwaway values.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run llms      # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI fails when it is stale)
```

`npm test` needs PostgreSQL (`PG_BIN`) and PgBouncer (`PGBOUNCER_BIN` or on PATH) for the integration
part; without them it is skipped locally. CI installs both and sets `REQUIRE_PGBOUNCER=1`. As root,
the servers run as `PG_TEST_USER` (default `nobody`).

## Repository rules

`main` takes pull requests only: squash merge, 1 code-owner review (`@BackStacked`), the `ci` check
required. Rules come from `mgpl-diagnostics/.github` (`scripts/protect-repos.mjs`).

## Licence

## File: llms.txt

# @mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit

> Reusable PgBouncer setup for the MGPL Diagnostics services (Node.js ≥ 20, PgBouncer ≥ 1.21): env-driven pgbouncer.ini, SCRAM/MD5 userlists, auth_query SQL, a docker-compose service, TLS options, a credential-free readiness probe and the `mgpl-pgbouncer` CLI. No runtime dependencies. Used in front of PostgreSQL by the api server and worker (db-kit's PostgreSQL backend).

Key facts for agents:
- `defineConfig({ databases: [{ name, host, port?, dbname?, poolSize?, poolMode? }], ... })` fills defaults (transaction pooling, scram-sha-256, 0.0.0.0:6432, default_pool_size 20, max_client_conn 500, max_prepared_statements 200, client TLS off, server TLS prefer) and throws PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG listing every problem.
- `renderIni(config)` → pgbouncer.ini (never a password). `configFromEnv(env)` reads PGBOUNCER_* (see `ENV_VARS`).
- Users: `usersFromEnv(env)` + `renderUserlist(entries, format = "scram")`; `scramVerifier(password)`, `alterRoleSql(user, verifier)` so PostgreSQL and PgBouncer share a verifier (needed for SCRAM pass-through); `PG_SHADOW_QUERY` + `userlistFromRows`; `authQuerySetupSql()` + `AUTH_QUERY` (auth user needs `format: "plain"`).
- `pgbouncerUrl(DATABASE_URL, { host: "pgbouncer" })` rewrites an app URL to go through PgBouncer.
- `renderCompose({ tlsDir?, publish?, dependsOn? })` → compose service (image `DEFAULT_IMAGE`, pg_isready health check).
- Health: `probePgBouncer`, `waitForPgBouncer` (PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE), `readiness({ query? })`.
- CLI: `mgpl-pgbouncer render|verifier|auth-setup|compose|check`.
- Errors: `PgBouncerError.code` = PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG, PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV, PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL, PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER, PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE; `problems` lists each issue.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): where it is used, adopting it in a service, defaults, environment, auth, TLS, health, CLI
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): map and rules

## Source

- [src/config.ts](src/config.ts): configuration, defaults, checks
- [src/ini.ts](src/ini.ts): pgbouncer.ini
- [src/env.ts](src/env.ts): environment variables
- [src/userlist.ts](src/userlist.ts): SCRAM, MD5, userlist, SQL helpers
- [src/compose.ts](src/compose.ts): docker-compose service
- [src/health.ts](src/health.ts): probe, wait, readiness
- [src/cli.ts](src/cli.ts): the CLI

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: scripts/test.ts

```ts
// pgbouncer-kit checks: configuration, ini, environment, userlists, URLs, compose, the probe, the CLI,
// and real PostgreSQL + PgBouncer: SCRAM pass-through with our verifiers, auth_query, transaction
// pooling with prepared statements, and the CLI's files running a real PgBouncer.
// Binaries: PG_BIN (folder with initdb/postgres; default the newest /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin) and
// PGBOUNCER_BIN (default `pgbouncer` on PATH). Without them the integration part is skipped;
// CI sets REQUIRE_PGBOUNCER=1 so it never skips. As root, servers run as PG_TEST_USER (default nobody).
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn, spawnSync, type ChildProcess } from "node:child_process";
import { chmodSync, chownSync, existsSync, mkdtempSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createServer, type AddressInfo } from "node:net";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import pg from "pg";
import {
  AUTH_QUERY,
  DEFAULT_CONFIG,
  DEFAULT_IMAGE,
  ENV_VARS,
  PgBouncerError,
  alterRoleSql,
  authQuerySetupSql,
  composeService,
  configFromEnv,
  defineConfig,
  md5Secret,
  parsePostgresUrl,
  parseScramVerifier,
  parseUserlist,
  pgbouncerUrl,
  probePgBouncer,
  readiness,
  renderCompose,
  renderIni,
  renderUserlist,
  saslprep,
  scramVerifier,
  secretFormatFromEnv,
  userlistFromRows,
  usersFromEnv,
  verifyScram,
  waitForPgBouncer,
  type PgBouncerErrorCode,
} from "../src/index";

let passed = 0;
let skipped = 0;
const failures: string[] = [];
async function check(name: string, fn: () => unknown): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await fn();
    passed++;
  } catch (e) {
    failures.push(`✗ ${name}\n    ${(e as Error).stack?.split("\n").slice(0, 5).join("\n    ")}`);
  }
}
function code(fn: () => unknown, expected: PgBouncerErrorCode): PgBouncerError {
  try {
    fn();
  } catch (e) {
    assert.ok(e instanceof PgBouncerError, `expected PgBouncerError, got ${String(e)}`);
    assert.equal(e.code, expected, e.message);
    return e;
  }
  assert.fail(`expected ${expected}`);
}
const db = { name: "mgpl", host: "postgres" };
const iniValue = (ini: string, key: string) => new RegExp(`^${key} = (.*)$`, "m").exec(ini)?.[1];

// ---- configuration ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("defaults: transaction pooling, scram, 6432, client TLS off, server TLS prefer", () => {
  const c = defineConfig({ databases: [db] });
  assert.equal(c.poolMode, "transaction");
  assert.equal(c.auth.type, "scram-sha-256");
  assert.equal(c.listenPort, 6432);
  assert.equal(c.defaultPoolSize, 20);
  assert.equal(c.maxPreparedStatements, 200);
  assert.equal(c.clientTls.mode, "disable");
  assert.equal(c.serverTls.mode, "prefer");
  assert.notEqual(c.adminUsers, DEFAULT_CONFIG.adminUsers, "lists are copied, not shared");
});

await check("defineConfig lists every problem at once", () => {
  const e = code(
    () =>
      defineConfig({
        databases: [{ name: "bad name", host: "h" }, { name: "pgbouncer", host: "h" }],
        poolMode: "sometimes" as never,
        listenPort: 70000,
        minPoolSize: 50,
        auth: { type: "trust" as never },
      }),
    "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG",
  );
  assert.ok(e.problems.length >= 5, e.problems.join("; "));
  for (const bit of ["databases[0].name", "reserved", "poolMode", "listenPort", "minPoolSize", "auth.type"]) {
    assert.ok(e.problems.some((p) => p.includes(bit)), `missing problem about ${bit}`);
  }
});

await check("no databases, duplicates and passwords in database entries are refused", () => {
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [] }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db, db] }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  const e = code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [{ ...db, password: "x" } as never] }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  assert.match(e.message, /userlist/);
});

await check("values cannot inject lines or settings", () => {
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [{ name: "a", host: "h\nlisten_port = 1" }] }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [{ name: "a", host: "h port=1" }] }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], serverResetQuery: "DISCARD ALL\nauth_type = trust" }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], extra: { auth_type: "trust" } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], extra: { client_tls_sslmode: "disable" } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], extra: { "bad key": 1 } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], adminUsers: ["a b"] }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
});

await check("TLS rules: client TLS needs cert+key, verify modes need a CA, cert auth needs client TLS", () => {
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], clientTls: { mode: "require" } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], serverTls: { mode: "verify-full" } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], serverTls: { mode: "prefer", certFile: "/c" } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], auth: { type: "cert" } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  defineConfig({
    databases: [db],
    clientTls: { mode: "require", certFile: "/tls/server.crt", keyFile: "/tls/server.key" },
    serverTls: { mode: "verify-full", caFile: "/tls/ca.crt" },
  });
});

await check("auth_query needs an auth user", () => {
  code(() => defineConfig({ databases: [db], auth: { query: AUTH_QUERY } }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  defineConfig({ databases: [db], auth: { query: AUTH_QUERY, user: "pgbouncer_auth" } });
  defineConfig({ databases: [{ ...db, authUser: "pgbouncer_auth" }], auth: { query: AUTH_QUERY } });

await check("ENV_VARS documents every variable the code reads", () => {

  for (const side of ["CLIENT", "SERVER"]) for (const s of ["SSLMODE", "CERT_FILE", "KEY_FILE", "CA_FILE", "PROTOCOLS", "CIPHERS"]) read.add(`PGBOUNCER_${side}_TLS_${s}`);
  for (const v of read) if (!v.endsWith("_") && !/^PGBOUNCER_(BAD_|UNREACHABLE)/.test(v)) assert.ok(v in ENV_VARS, `${v} is missing from ENV_VARS`);

});

// ---- userlist --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("md5Secret matches PostgreSQL's md5(password || user)", () => {
  // md5("pencil" + "user")
  assert.equal(md5Secret("user", "pencil"), "md520c46e3762c864548e296b33c3406aa9");
  assert.notEqual(md5Secret("user", "pencil"), md5Secret("user2", "pencil"));
});

await check("scramVerifier: format, salt reuse reproduces, verifyScram", () => {
  const v = scramVerifier("pencil");
  const p = parseScramVerifier(v)!;
  assert.equal(p.iterations, 4096);
  assert.equal(p.salt.length, 16);
  assert.equal(p.storedKey.length, 32);
  assert.equal(scramVerifier("pencil", { salt: p.salt }), v);
  assert.notEqual(scramVerifier("pencil"), v, "random salt");
  assert.ok(verifyScram("pencil", v));
  assert.ok(!verifyScram("pencil2", v));
  assert.ok(!verifyScram("pencil", "nonsense"));
  assert.equal(parseScramVerifier("SCRAM-SHA-256$x"), null);
});

await check("scramVerifier: RFC 7677 keys for user/pencil", async () => {
  // RFC 7677 §3: salt W22ZaJ0SNY7soEsUEjb6gQ==, 4096 iterations; ServerSignature there verifies with this ServerKey.
  const v = scramVerifier("pencil", { salt: Buffer.from("W22ZaJ0SNY7soEsUEjb6gQ==", "base64") });
  const p = parseScramVerifier(v)!;
  // AuthMessage from the RFC; ServerSignature = HMAC(ServerKey, AuthMessage) = 6rriTRBi23WpRR/wtup+mMhUZUn/dB5nLTJRsjl95G4=
  const auth = "n=user,r=rOprNGfwEbeRWgbNEkqO,r=rOprNGfwEbeRWgbNEkqO%hvYDpWUa2RaTCAfuxFIlj)hNlF$k0,s=W22ZaJ0SNY7soEsUEjb6gQ==,i=4096,c=biws,r=rOprNGfwEbeRWgbNEkqO%hvYDpWUa2RaTCAfuxFIlj)hNlF$k0";
  const { createHmac } = await import("node:crypto");
  assert.equal(createHmac("sha256", p.serverKey).update(auth).digest("base64"), "6rriTRBi23WpRR/wtup+mMhUZUn/dB5nLTJRsjl95G4=");
});

await check("saslprep: ASCII unchanged, non-ASCII spaces mapped, soft hyphen dropped, NFKC", () => {
  assert.equal(saslprep("pencil"), "pencil");
  assert.equal(saslprep("a b"), "a b");
  assert.equal(saslprep("I­X"), "IX");
  assert.equal(saslprep("Ⅸ"), "IX");
  assert.equal(saslprep("a\u0007b"), "a\u0007b", "prohibited → raw bytes, as PostgreSQL does");
});

await check("renderUserlist / parseUserlist: quoting, formats, duplicates, round trip", () => {
  const v = scramVerifier("x");
  const text = renderUserlist([
    { user: "app", secret: v },
    { user: "plain", secret: 'pa"ss' },
  ], "plain");
  assert.equal(text, `"app" "${v}"\n"plain" "pa""ss"\n`);
  assert.deepEqual(parseUserlist(`; comment\n\n${text}`), [{ user: "app", secret: v }, { user: "plain", secret: 'pa"ss' }]);
  const scram = parseUserlist(renderUserlist([{ user: "app", secret: "pw" }]))[0]!;
  assert.ok(verifyScram("pw", scram.secret), "plain passwords become SCRAM by default");
  assert.equal(parseUserlist(renderUserlist([{ user: "app", secret: "pw" }], "md5"))[0]!.secret, md5Secret("app", "pw"));
  code(() => renderUserlist([{ user: "a", secret: "1" }, { user: "a", secret: "2" }]), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  code(() => renderUserlist([{ user: 'a"b', secret: "1" }]), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  code(() => renderUserlist([{ user: "a", secret: "x\ny" }]), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  code(() => renderUserlist([{ user: "a", secret: "SCRAM-SHA-256$broken" }]), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  code(() => renderUserlist([{ user: "a", secret: "" }]), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  assert.equal(renderUserlist([]), "");
});

await check("userlistFromRows, alterRoleSql, authQuerySetupSql", () => {
  const v = scramVerifier("x");
  assert.equal(userlistFromRows([{ usename: "app", passwd: v }, { usename: "nologin", passwd: null }]), `"app" "${v}"\n`);
  assert.equal(alterRoleSql("app", v), `ALTER ROLE "app" PASSWORD '${v}';`);
  code(() => alterRoleSql("app", "plaintext"), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  code(() => alterRoleSql("a'b", v), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER");
  const sql = authQuerySetupSql();
  assert.match(sql, /SECURITY DEFINER/);
  assert.match(sql, /NOT usesuper/);
  assert.match(sql, /REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION pgbouncer\.user_lookup\(text\) FROM PUBLIC/);
});

// ---- URLs ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("parsePostgresUrl and pgbouncerUrl", () => {
  const p = parsePostgresUrl("postgresql://app:p%40ss@[::1]:5433/mgpl?sslmode=require&application_name=api");
  assert.deepEqual(p, { host: "::1", port: 5433, database: "mgpl", user: "app", password: "p@ss", params: { sslmode: "require", application_name: "api" } });
  assert.equal(parsePostgresUrl("postgres://app@h").database, "app");
  code(() => parsePostgresUrl("mysql://h/d"), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL");
  code(() => parsePostgresUrl("not a url"), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL");
  assert.equal(
    pgbouncerUrl("postgres://app:p%40ss@db.internal:5432/mgpl?application_name=api", { host: "pgbouncer" }),
    "postgres://app:p%40ss@pgbouncer:6432/mgpl?application_name=api",
  );
  assert.equal(pgbouncerUrl("postgres://a:b@h/d", { host: "::1", port: 7000, database: "alias" }), "postgres://a:b@[::1]:7000/alias");
});

// ---- compose ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("composeService / renderCompose", () => {
  const { name, service } = composeService();
  assert.equal(name, "pgbouncer");
  assert.equal(service.image, DEFAULT_IMAGE);
  assert.equal(service.ports, undefined, "not published by default");
  assert.deepEqual(service.depends_on, { postgres: { condition: "service_healthy" } });
  assert.deepEqual(service.healthcheck.test, ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-p", "6432"]);
  assert.ok(service.volumes.every((v) => v.endsWith(":ro")));
  const y = renderCompose({ name: "db-pool", port: 7432, publish: "127.0.0.1:7432", dependsOn: [], tlsDir: "./tls", networks: ["backend"] });
  assert.match(y, /^services:\n {2}db-pool:\n/m);
  assert.match(y, /- "127\.0\.0\.1:7432:7432"/);
  assert.match(y, /- "\.\/tls:\/etc\/pgbouncer\/tls:ro"/);
  assert.match(y, /retries: 10/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(y, /depends_on/);
  code(() => composeService({ name: "Bad Name" }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => composeService({ publish: "0.0.0.0:x" }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
  code(() => composeService({ configDir: "./a:b" }), "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG");
});

// ---- probe against fake servers ----------------------------------------------------------------

async function fakeServer(answer: (s: import("node:net").Socket) => void): Promise<{ port: number; close: () => Promise<void> }> {
  const server = createServer(answer);
  await new Promise<void>((r) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", r));
  return { port: (server.address() as AddressInfo).port, close: () => new Promise((r) => server.close(() => r())) };
}
async function freePort(): Promise<number> {
  const s = await fakeServer((c) => c.destroy());
  await s.close();
  return s.port;
}

await check("probePgBouncer: N and S answers, wrong protocol, closed port, timeout", async () => {
  const seen: Buffer[] = [];
  const n = await fakeServer((s) => s.once("data", (b) => (seen.push(b), s.end("N"))));
  const r = await probePgBouncer({ port: n.port });
  assert.equal(r.ok, true);
  assert.equal(r.tls, false);
  assert.deepEqual([...seen[0]!], [0, 0, 0, 8, 4, 210, 22, 47]);
  await n.close();
  const s = await fakeServer((c) => c.once("data", () => c.end("S")));
  assert.equal((await probePgBouncer({ port: s.port })).tls, true);
  await s.close();
  const http = await fakeServer((c) => c.once("data", () => c.end("HTTP/1.1 400\r\n\r\n")));
  assert.deepEqual({ ...(await probePgBouncer({ port: http.port })), latencyMs: 0 }, { ok: false, tls: null, error: "not a PostgreSQL protocol answer", latencyMs: 0 });
  await http.close();
  assert.equal((await probePgBouncer({ port: await freePort() })).error, "ECONNREFUSED");
  const silent = await fakeServer((c) => void c.resume());
  const t = await probePgBouncer({ port: silent.port, timeoutMs: 100 });
  assert.equal(t.ok, false);
  assert.match(t.error!, /no answer within 100 ms/);
  await silent.close();
});

await check("waitForPgBouncer retries, then gives up with PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE", async () => {
  const port = await freePort();
  setTimeout(() => void fakeServer((c) => c.once("data", () => c.end("N"))).then((s) => setTimeout(() => void s.close(), 2000)), 150);
  // the fake server listens on a new port, so this one must time out
  await assert.rejects(waitForPgBouncer({ port, waitMs: 300, intervalMs: 50 }), (e: unknown) => e instanceof PgBouncerError && e.code === "PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE");
  const later = await fakeServer((c) => c.once("data", () => c.end("N")));
  const r = await waitForPgBouncer({ port: later.port, waitMs: 1000 });
  assert.equal(r.ok, true);
  await later.close();
});

await check("readiness: probe only, query ok, query failure and timeout summarised", async () => {
  const s = await fakeServer((c) => c.once("data", () => c.end("N")));
  assert.equal((await readiness({ port: s.port })()).ok, true);
  const good = await readiness({ port: s.port, query: async () => 1 })();
  assert.equal(good.query?.ok, true);
  const bad = await readiness({ port: s.port, query: async () => { throw new Error("password authentication failed\nDETAIL"); } })();
  assert.deepEqual([bad.ok, bad.query?.error], [false, "password authentication failed"]);
  const slow = await readiness({ port: s.port, queryTimeoutMs: 50, query: () => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)) })();
  assert.match(slow.query!.error!, /longer than 50 ms/);
  await s.close();
  const down = await readiness({ port: await freePort(), query: async () => assert.fail("must not run") })();
  assert.deepEqual([down.ok, down.query], [false, undefined]);
});

// ---- real PostgreSQL + PgBouncer -------------------------------------------------------------

function findPgBin(): string | null {
  if (process.env.PG_BIN) return process.env.PG_BIN;
  const root = "/usr/lib/postgresql";
  if (!existsSync(root)) return null;
  const versions = readdirSync(root).filter((v) => existsSync(join(root, v, "bin", "postgres"))).sort((a, b) => Number(b) - Number(a));
  return versions[0] ? join(root, versions[0], "bin") : null;
}
function findPgBouncer(): string | null {
  if (process.env.PGBOUNCER_BIN) return process.env.PGBOUNCER_BIN;
  const r = spawnSync("sh", ["-c", "command -v pgbouncer || ls /usr/sbin/pgbouncer 2>/dev/null"], { encoding: "utf8" });
  return r.stdout.trim().split("\n")[0] || null;
}

const pgBin = findPgBin();
const bouncerBin = findPgBouncer();
const procs: ChildProcess[] = [];
let work = "";

if (!pgBin || !bouncerBin) {
  if (process.env.REQUIRE_PGBOUNCER === "1") failures.push(`✗ PostgreSQL (${pgBin ?? "missing"}) and PgBouncer (${bouncerBin ?? "missing"}) are required`);
  else {
    console.log("PostgreSQL or PgBouncer not found: skipping the integration checks (set PG_BIN / PGBOUNCER_BIN)");
    skipped++;
  }
} else {
  const asRoot = process.getuid?.() === 0;
  const runAs = process.env.PG_TEST_USER ?? "nobody";
  const ids = asRoot ? spawnSync("id", ["-u", runAs], { encoding: "utf8" }).stdout.trim() : "";
  const uid = Number(ids);
  const gid = asRoot ? Number(spawnSync("id", ["-g", runAs], { encoding: "utf8" }).stdout.trim()) : 0;
  const wrap = (cmd: string, args: string[]): [string, string[]] => (asRoot ? ["runuser", ["-u", runAs, "--", cmd, ...args]] : [cmd, args]);
  const own = (p: string) => asRoot && chownSync(p, uid, gid);
  const sh = (cmd: string, args: string[]) => {
    const [c, a] = wrap(cmd, args);
    const r = spawnSync(c, a, { encoding: "utf8" });
    if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`${cmd} failed: ${r.stderr || r.stdout}`);
  };
  const start = (cmd: string, args: string[], label: string) => {
    const [c, a] = wrap(cmd, args);
    const p = spawn(c, a, { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] });
    let log = "";
    p.stdout!.on("data", (b) => (log += b));
    p.stderr!.on("data", (b) => (log += b));
    procs.push(p);
    return { proc: p, log: () => `${label}:\n${log}` };
  };

  work = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "pgbouncer-kit-"));
  chmodSync(work, 0o755);
  own(work);
  const pgData = join(work, "pgdata");
  const superPw = "super-" + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2);
  writeFileSync(join(work, "pw"), superPw);
  own(join(work, "pw"));
  const pgPort = await freePort();
  const bouncerPort = await freePort();
  const authPort = await freePort();
  const cliPort = await freePort();

  await check("integration: PostgreSQL starts with SCRAM", async () => {
    sh(join(pgBin, "initdb"), ["-D", pgData, "-U", "postgres", "--auth=scram-sha-256", `--pwfile=${join(work, "pw")}`, "-E", "UTF8", "--no-instructions"]);
    start(join(pgBin, "postgres"), ["-D", pgData, "-p", String(pgPort), "-k", work, "-c", "listen_addresses=127.0.0.1"], "postgres");
    await waitForPgBouncer({ port: pgPort, waitMs: 20_000 });
  });

  const superClient = async (database = "postgres") => {
    for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
      const c = new pg.Client({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: pgPort, user: "postgres", password: superPw, database });
      try {
        await c.connect();
        return c;
      } catch (e) {
        await c.end().catch(() => undefined);
        if (i > 50) throw e;
        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200));
      }
    }
  };

  const appVerifier = scramVerifier("app-password");
  const authVerifier = scramVerifier("auth-password");

  await check("integration: our verifier equals PostgreSQL's for the same salt (ASCII and Unicode)", async () => {
    const c = await superClient();
    try {
      for (const pw of ["pencil", "pässwörd ⅨX", "a\u0007b"]) {
        await c.query(`DROP ROLE IF EXISTS probe; CREATE ROLE probe PASSWORD '${pw.replace(/'/g, "''")}'`);
        const { rows } = await c.query<{ rolpassword: string }>("SELECT rolpassword FROM pg_authid WHERE rolname = 'probe'");
        const server = rows[0]!.rolpassword;
        const parts = parseScramVerifier(server)!;
        assert.equal(scramVerifier(pw, { salt: parts.salt, iterations: parts.iterations }), server, `password ${JSON.stringify(pw)}`);
        assert.ok(verifyScram(pw, server));
      }
      await c.query("DROP ROLE probe");
      // set up the app and auth roles with verifiers made here
      await c.query(`CREATE ROLE app LOGIN; ${alterRoleSql("app", appVerifier)}`);
      await c.query("CREATE DATABASE mgpl OWNER app");
      await c.query("CREATE ROLE dynamic LOGIN PASSWORD 'dynamic-password'; GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE mgpl TO dynamic");
      const { rows } = await c.query<{ rolpassword: string }>("SELECT rolpassword FROM pg_authid WHERE rolname = 'app'");
      assert.equal(rows[0]!.rolpassword, appVerifier, "PostgreSQL stores the pre-hashed verifier as it is");
    } finally {
      await c.end();
    }
    const m = await superClient("mgpl");
    try {
      await m.query(authQuerySetupSql("pgbouncer_auth"));
      await m.query(authQuerySetupSql("pgbouncer_auth")); // idempotent
      await m.query(alterRoleSql("pgbouncer_auth", authVerifier));
      await m.query("GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE mgpl TO pgbouncer_auth");
    } finally {
      await m.end();
    }
  });

  const writeConfig = (dir: string, ini: string, users: string) => {
    writeFileSync(join(dir, "pgbouncer.ini"), ini);
    writeFileSync(join(dir, "userlist.txt"), users, { mode: 0o600 });
    own(join(dir, "pgbouncer.ini"));
    own(join(dir, "userlist.txt"));
  };
  const bouncerConfig = (port: number, file: string, auth: Record<string, string> = {}) =>
    renderIni({
      listenAddr: "127.0.0.1",
      listenPort: port,
      databases: [{ name: "mgpl", host: "127.0.0.1", port: pgPort }],
      auth: { file, ...auth },
      serverTls: { mode: "disable" },
      adminUsers: ["app"],
      extra: { unix_socket_dir: "" },
    });

  const connect = (port: number, user: string, password: string, database = "mgpl") =>
    new pg.Client({ host: "127.0.0.1", port, user, password, database, connectionTimeoutMillis: 5000 });

  await check("integration: PgBouncer with a SCRAM userlist passes through to PostgreSQL", async () => {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(work, "b1-"));
    chmodSync(dir, 0o755);
    own(dir);
    writeConfig(dir, bouncerConfig(bouncerPort, join(dir, "userlist.txt")), renderUserlist([{ user: "app", secret: appVerifier }]));
    const b = start(bouncerBin, [join(dir, "pgbouncer.ini")], "pgbouncer");
    try {
      await waitForPgBouncer({ port: bouncerPort, waitMs: 10_000 });
    } catch (e) {
      throw new Error(`${(e as Error).message}\n${b.log()}`);
    }
    const c = connect(bouncerPort, "app", "app-password");
    await c.connect();
    try {
      assert.equal((await c.query("SELECT 1 AS one")).rows[0].one, 1);
      // transaction pooling: work inside a transaction stays on one server connection
      await c.query("BEGIN");
      await c.query("CREATE TEMP TABLE t (n int) ON COMMIT DROP");
      await c.query("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (2)");
      assert.equal((await c.query("SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM t")).rows[0].n, 2);
      await c.query("COMMIT");
      // named protocol-level prepared statements (max_prepared_statements)
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        const r = await c.query({ name: "plus", text: "SELECT $1::int + 1 AS n", values: [i] });
        assert.equal(r.rows[0].n, i + 1);
      }
    } finally {
      await c.end();
    }
    const wrong = connect(bouncerPort, "app", "not-the-password");
    await assert.rejects(wrong.connect(), /password authentication failed|SASL/);
    await wrong.end().catch(() => undefined);
    // the admin console answers SHOW POOLS for admin_users
    const admin = connect(bouncerPort, "app", "app-password", "pgbouncer");
    await admin.connect();
    try {
      const pools = await admin.query<{ database: string }>({ text: "SHOW POOLS", queryMode: "simple" } as pg.QueryConfig);
      assert.ok(pools.rows.some((r) => r.database === "mgpl"));
      assert.equal(iniValue(bouncerConfig(1, "x"), "pool_mode"), "transaction");
    } finally {
      await admin.end();
    }
    const ready = await readiness({ port: bouncerPort, query: async () => {
      const q = connect(bouncerPort, "app", "app-password");
      await q.connect();
      try {
        return await q.query("SELECT 1");
      } finally {
        await q.end();
      }
    } })();
    assert.equal(ready.ok, true, JSON.stringify(ready));
  });

  await check("integration: auth_query finds users that are not in the userlist (never superusers)", async () => {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(work, "b2-"));
    chmodSync(dir, 0o755);
    own(dir);
    writeConfig(
      dir,
      bouncerConfig(authPort, join(dir, "userlist.txt"), { query: AUTH_QUERY, user: "pgbouncer_auth", dbname: "mgpl" }),
      renderUserlist([{ user: "pgbouncer_auth", secret: "auth-password", format: "plain" }]),
    );
    const b = start(bouncerBin, [join(dir, "pgbouncer.ini")], "pgbouncer auth_query");
    try {
      await waitForPgBouncer({ port: authPort, waitMs: 10_000 });
    } catch (e) {
      throw new Error(`${(e as Error).message}\n${b.log()}`);
    }
    const c = connect(authPort, "dynamic", "dynamic-password");
    await c.connect();
    try {
      assert.equal((await c.query("SELECT current_user AS u")).rows[0].u, "dynamic");
    } finally {
      await c.end();
    }
    const su = connect(authPort, "postgres", superPw);
    await assert.rejects(su.connect());
    await su.end().catch(() => undefined);
  });

  await check("integration: the CLI renders files from PGBOUNCER_* variables that a real PgBouncer runs", async () => {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(join(work, "cli-"));
    chmodSync(dir, 0o755);
    own(dir);
    const out = join(dir, "conf");
    const env = {
      ...process.env,
      PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL: `postgres://127.0.0.1:${pgPort}/mgpl?sslmode=disable`,
      PGBOUNCER_USERS: `app:${appVerifier}`,
      PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_ADDR: "127.0.0.1",
      PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_PORT: String(cliPort),
      PGBOUNCER_AUTH_FILE: join(out, "userlist.txt"),
      PGBOUNCER_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE: "4",
    };
    const tsx = join(process.cwd(), "node_modules", ".bin", "tsx");
    const r = spawnSync(tsx, ["src/cli.ts", "render", "--out", out], { env, encoding: "utf8" });
    assert.equal(r.status, 0, r.stderr);
    assert.doesNotMatch(r.stdout, /SCRAM|password/i, "prints paths, not secrets");
    assert.equal(statSync(join(out, "userlist.txt")).mode & 0o777, 0o600);
    const ini = readFileSync(join(out, "pgbouncer.ini"), "utf8");
    assert.equal(iniValue(ini, "default_pool_size"), "4");
    assert.equal(iniValue(ini, "server_tls_sslmode"), "disable");
    // the compose image's unix socket dir does not exist here
    writeFileSync(join(out, "pgbouncer.ini"), `${ini}\nunix_socket_dir =\n`);
    for (const f of ["", "pgbouncer.ini", "userlist.txt"]) own(join(out, f));
    const b = start(bouncerBin, [join(out, "pgbouncer.ini")], "pgbouncer cli");
    try {
      await waitForPgBouncer({ port: cliPort, waitMs: 10_000 });
    } catch (e) {
      throw new Error(`${(e as Error).message}\n${b.log()}`);
    }
    const c = connect(cliPort, "app", "app-password");
    await c.connect();
    try {
      assert.equal((await c.query("SELECT current_database() AS d")).rows[0].d, "mgpl");
    } finally {
      await c.end();
    }
    const check = spawnSync(tsx, ["src/cli.ts", "check", "--port", String(cliPort)], { encoding: "utf8" });
    assert.equal(check.status, 0, check.stderr);
    const verifier = spawnSync(tsx, ["src/cli.ts", "verifier", "app"], { input: "app-password\n", encoding: "utf8" });
    const [v, sql] = verifier.stdout.trim().split("\n");
    assert.ok(verifyScram("app-password", v!));
    assert.equal(sql, alterRoleSql("app", v!));
    const bad = spawnSync(tsx, ["src/cli.ts", "render", "--out", join(dir, "x")], { env: { PATH: process.env.PATH }, encoding: "utf8" });
    assert.equal(bad.status, 1);
    assert.match(bad.stderr, /PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV/);
  });
}

// ---- done ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

for (const p of procs) p.kill("SIGTERM");
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
if (work) rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });

if (failures.length) {
  console.error(failures.join("\n"));
  console.error(`\n${failures.length} failed, ${passed} passed`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(`${passed} checks passed${skipped ? " (integration skipped)" : ""}`);
process.exit(0);
```

## File: src/cli.ts

```ts
// mgpl-pgbouncer: the kit from a shell (container entrypoints, CI, one-off setup).
// It prints file paths and verifiers, never a password.
import { chmodSync, chownSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { renderCompose } from "./compose";
import { configFromEnv, secretFormatFromEnv, usersFromEnv } from "./env";
import { isPgBouncerError } from "./errors";
import { waitForPgBouncer } from "./health";
import { renderIni } from "./ini";
import { alterRoleSql, authQuerySetupSql, renderUserlist, scramVerifier } from "./userlist";

const HELP = `mgpl-pgbouncer <command>

  render [--out DIR] [--chown UID[:GID]]
                                write pgbouncer.ini and userlist.txt (mode 600) from PGBOUNCER_* variables
                                (default DIR: ./pgbouncer; --chown 70 for the compose image's postgres user)
  verifier USER                 read a password from stdin; print its SCRAM verifier and the ALTER ROLE
                                statement that sets the same verifier on PostgreSQL
  auth-setup [AUTH_USER]        print the SQL for auth_query (default role: pgbouncer_auth)
  compose [--name N] [--port P] [--config-dir D] [--tls-dir D] [--publish [IP:]PORT] [--image I]
          [--depends-on a,b]    print a docker-compose service (use --depends-on "" for none)
  check [--host H] [--port P] [--wait MS]
                                exit 0 once PgBouncer answers, 1 otherwise
`;

function flags(args: string[]): Record<string, string> {
  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
    const a = args[i]!;
    if (!a.startsWith("--")) continue;
    const next = args[i + 1];
    out[a.slice(2)] = next !== undefined && !next.startsWith("--") ? (i++, next) : "";
  }
  return out;
}

const int = (v: string | undefined) => (v === undefined || v === "" ? undefined : Number(v));

async function main(argv: string[]): Promise<number> {
  const [cmd, ...rest] = argv;
  const f = flags(rest);
  switch (cmd) {
    case "render": {
      const out = f.out || "./pgbouncer";
      const config = configFromEnv(process.env);
      const ini = renderIni(config);
      const users = renderUserlist(usersFromEnv(process.env), secretFormatFromEnv(process.env));
      mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(join(out, "pgbouncer.ini"), ini, { mode: 0o644 });
      const userlist = join(out, "userlist.txt");
      writeFileSync(userlist, users, { mode: 0o600 });
      chmodSync(userlist, 0o600);
      if (f.chown) {
        // the compose image runs as postgres (uid 70) and must be able to read the userlist
        const m = /^(\d+)(?::(\d+))?$/.exec(f.chown);
        if (!m) throw new Error("--chown takes UID or UID:GID");
        chownSync(userlist, Number(m[1]), Number(m[2] ?? m[1]));
      }
      console.log(`wrote ${join(out, "pgbouncer.ini")} and ${userlist} (${users ? users.trim().split("\n").length : 0} users)`);
      return 0;
    }
    case "verifier": {
      const user = rest[0];
      if (!user || user.startsWith("--")) break;
      const password = readFileSync(0, "utf8").replace(/\r?\n$/, "");
      const v = scramVerifier(password);
      console.log(v);
      console.log(alterRoleSql(user, v));
      return 0;
    }
    case "auth-setup":
      process.stdout.write(authQuerySetupSql(rest[0] && !rest[0].startsWith("--") ? rest[0] : undefined));
      return 0;
    case "compose":
      process.stdout.write(
        renderCompose({
          name: f.name || undefined,
          port: int(f.port),
          configDir: f["config-dir"] || undefined,
          tlsDir: f["tls-dir"] || undefined,
          publish: f.publish || undefined,
          image: f.image || undefined,
          dependsOn: "depends-on" in f ? f["depends-on"]!.split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean) : undefined,
        }),
      );
      return 0;
    case "check": {
      const r = await waitForPgBouncer({ host: f.host || undefined, port: int(f.port), waitMs: int(f.wait) ?? 0 });
      console.log(`ok (${r.latencyMs} ms, tls ${r.tls ? "offered" : "not offered"})`);
      return 0;
    }
  }
  process.stderr.write(HELP);
  return cmd === "help" || cmd === "--help" ? 0 : 2;
}

main(process.argv.slice(2)).then(
  (code) => process.exit(code),
  (e) => {
    console.error(isPgBouncerError(e) ? `${e.code}: ${e.message}` : (e as Error).message);
    process.exit(1);
  },
);
```


---

## File: src/compose.ts

```ts
import { PgBouncerError } from "./errors";

/**
 * Pinned image (Alpine, runs as `postgres`, ships `pg_isready`). It uses a mounted
 * /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini as it is; do not also set its DATABASE_URL variables.
 */
export const DEFAULT_IMAGE = "edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0";

export interface ComposeOptions {
  /** Service name. Default `pgbouncer`. */
  name?: string;
  /** Default `DEFAULT_IMAGE`. */
  image?: string;
  /** PgBouncer's `listenPort`. Default 6432. */
  port?: number;
  /** Host folder holding pgbouncer.ini and userlist.txt (from `mgpl-pgbouncer render`). Default `./pgbouncer`. */
  configDir?: string;
  /** Host folder with TLS files, mounted read-only at /etc/pgbouncer/tls. */
  tlsDir?: string;
  /**
   * Publish the port on the host, e.g. `"127.0.0.1:6432"`. Default: not published, so only
   * services on the same compose network reach it.
   */
  publish?: string;
  /** Services to wait for (healthy). Default `["postgres"]`; `[]` for a managed database. */
  dependsOn?: string[];
  /** Compose networks to join. */
  networks?: string[];
  /** Default `unless-stopped`. */
  restart?: string;
}

export interface ComposeService {
  image: string;
  restart: string;
  volumes: string[];
  ports?: string[];
  depends_on?: Record<string, { condition: "service_healthy" }>;
  networks?: string[];
  healthcheck: { test: string[]; interval: string; timeout: string; retries: number; start_period: string };
}

const NAME = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*$/;

/** The compose service definition, as an object (merge it into your own file however you like). */
export function composeService(opts: ComposeOptions = {}): { name: string; service: ComposeService } {
  const name = opts.name ?? "pgbouncer";
  const port = opts.port ?? 6432;
  const dir = opts.configDir ?? "./pgbouncer";
  for (const n of [name, ...(opts.dependsOn ?? []), ...(opts.networks ?? [])]) {
    if (!NAME.test(n)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG", `"${n}" is not a valid compose service or network name`);
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG", "port must be 1-65535");
  if (opts.publish !== undefined && !/^(\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}:)?\d{1,5}$/.test(opts.publish)) {
    throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG", 'publish must be "<host port>" or "<ip>:<host port>"');
  }
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
  const bad = (v: string | undefined, colon: boolean) => v !== undefined && (!v || /[\u0000-\u0020\u007f]/.test(v) || (colon && v.includes(":")));
  if (bad(opts.image, false) || bad(opts.restart, true)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG", "image and restart must be single words");
  if (bad(opts.configDir, true) || bad(opts.tlsDir, true)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG", "configDir and tlsDir must be paths without spaces or colons");
  const service: ComposeService = {
    image: opts.image ?? DEFAULT_IMAGE,
    restart: opts.restart ?? "unless-stopped",
    volumes: [
      `${dir}/pgbouncer.ini:/etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini:ro`,
      `${dir}/userlist.txt:/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt:ro`,
      ...(opts.tlsDir ? [`${opts.tlsDir}:/etc/pgbouncer/tls:ro`] : []),
    ],
    healthcheck: {
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-p", String(port)],
      interval: "5s",
      timeout: "3s",
      retries: 10,
      start_period: "5s",
    },
  };
  if (opts.publish) service.ports = [`${opts.publish}:${port}`];
  const deps = opts.dependsOn ?? ["postgres"];
  if (deps.length) service.depends_on = Object.fromEntries(deps.map((d) => [d, { condition: "service_healthy" as const }]));
  if (opts.networks?.length) service.networks = [...opts.networks];
  return { name, service };
}

function yaml(value: unknown, indent: number): string {
  const pad = "  ".repeat(indent);
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((v) => `\n${pad}- ${scalar(v)}`).join("");
  if (value && typeof value === "object") {
    return Object.entries(value)
      .map(([k, v]) => (v && typeof v === "object" ? `\n${pad}${k}:${yaml(v, indent + 1)}` : `\n${pad}${k}: ${scalar(v)}`))
      .join("");
  }
  return ` ${scalar(value)}`;
}
const scalar = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === "number" ? String(v) : JSON.stringify(String(v)));

/** The service as a docker-compose YAML fragment (`services:` block), ready to save or paste. */
export function renderCompose(opts: ComposeOptions = {}): string {
  const { name, service } = composeService(opts);
  return `# Generated by @mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit\nservices:\n  ${name}:${yaml(service, 2)}\n`;
}
```

## File: src/config.ts

```ts
import { PgBouncerError } from "./errors";

export type PoolMode = "session" | "transaction" | "statement";
/** `trust` and `any` are accepted by PgBouncer but refused here: every client must authenticate. */
export type AuthType = "scram-sha-256" | "md5" | "plain" | "cert" | "hba";
export type TlsMode = "disable" | "allow" | "prefer" | "require" | "verify-ca" | "verify-full";

/** One entry of the [databases] section: a name clients connect to, and where it really lives. */
export interface DatabaseTarget {
  /** The name clients put in their URL. `*` is the fallback for any name. */
  name: string;
  host: string;
  /** Default 5432. */
  port?: number;
  /** The database on the server; default: `name` (or the client's name for `*`). */
  dbname?: string;
  /**
   * Forces the server-side user. Leave it out so PgBouncer logs in as the client's user (the
   * default, and what SCRAM pass-through needs). Never put a password here: passwords live in the userlist.
   */
  user?: string;
  /** Overrides the global `poolMode` for this database. */
  poolMode?: PoolMode;
  /** Overrides `defaultPoolSize`. */
  poolSize?: number;
  /** Overrides `minPoolSize`. */
  minPoolSize?: number;
  /** Overrides `reservePoolSize`. */
  reservePoolSize?: number;
  /** Overrides `maxDbConnections`. */
  maxDbConnections?: number;
  /** `auth_user` for this database's `auth_query`. */
  authUser?: string;
}

/** TLS for one side: `client` = apps → PgBouncer, `server` = PgBouncer → PostgreSQL. */
export interface TlsSide {
  mode: TlsMode;
  certFile?: string;
  keyFile?: string;
  caFile?: string;
  /** PgBouncer's `*_tls_protocols`, e.g. `"secure"` (TLS 1.2 + 1.3, PgBouncer's default) or `"tlsv1.3"`. */
  protocols?: string;
  /** OpenSSL cipher list; PgBouncer's default (`fast`) when left out. */
  ciphers?: string;
}

export interface AuthConfig {
  /** Default `scram-sha-256`. */
  type: AuthType;
  /** Default `/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt`. */
  file: string;
  /**
   * Looks users up in PostgreSQL instead of (or besides) the userlist, as `authUser`.
   * `authQuerySetupSql()` creates a safe lookup function for it.
   */
  query?: string;
  /** The user `query` runs as. It must itself be in the userlist. */
  user?: string;
  /** Database `query` runs in (PgBouncer ≥ 1.20); default: the database the client asked for. */
  dbname?: string;
  /** `hba` auth only: path of the pg_hba-style file. */
  hbaFile?: string;
}

export interface PgBouncerConfig {
  /** Default `0.0.0.0` (inside a container network). Use `127.0.0.1` on a shared host. */
  listenAddr: string;
  /** Default 6432. */
  listenPort: number;
  databases: DatabaseTarget[];
  /**
   * Default `transaction`: a server connection is held only during a transaction. Clients must not
   * rely on session state (`SET` outside a transaction, session advisory locks, `LISTEN`, temp
   * tables across transactions). db-kit's PostgreSQL backend is transaction-safe.
   */
  poolMode: PoolMode;
  /** Default 500. */
  maxClientConn: number;
  /** Server connections per user+database pair. Default 20. */
  defaultPoolSize: number;
  /** Default 0. */
  minPoolSize: number;
  /** Extra connections allowed when a client waits longer than `reservePoolTimeout`. Default 5. */
  reservePoolSize: number;
  /** Seconds. Default 3. */
  reservePoolTimeout: number;
  /** Cap per database across users; 0 = no cap (PgBouncer's default). Default 0. */
  maxDbConnections: number;
  /** Protocol-level prepared statements in transaction mode (PgBouncer ≥ 1.21). 0 = off. Default 200. */
  maxPreparedStatements: number;
  auth: AuthConfig;
  /** May run admin commands on the `pgbouncer` console. Default none. */
  adminUsers: string[];
  /** May run read-only `SHOW` commands on the console. Default none. */
  statsUsers: string[];
  /** Default `DISCARD ALL` (used in session mode). */
  serverResetQuery: string;
  /** Seconds. Default 3600. */
  serverLifetime: number;
  /** Seconds. Default 600. */
  serverIdleTimeout: number;
  /** Seconds. Default 15. */
  serverConnectTimeout: number;
  /** Seconds a client may wait for a server connection. Default 120. */
  queryWaitTimeout: number;
  /** Seconds; 0 = off. Default 0. */
  clientIdleTimeout: number;
  /** Seconds a server connection may sit idle inside a transaction; 0 = off. Default 0. */
  idleTransactionTimeout: number;
  /** Startup parameters PgBouncer ignores instead of refusing. Default `extra_float_digits`. */
  ignoreStartupParameters: string[];
  /** Default false: connections and disconnections are not logged (busy pools are noisy). */
  logConnections: boolean;
  /** Default true. */
  logPoolerErrors: boolean;
  /** Default `{ mode: "disable" }`: apps reach PgBouncer over the private network. */
  clientTls: TlsSide;
  /** Default `{ mode: "prefer" }` (PgBouncer's default). Use `verify-full` for managed PostgreSQL. */
  serverTls: TlsSide;
  /** Any other [pgbouncer] setting, written last. Keys are checked; values are written as they are. */
  extra: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
}

export type PgBouncerConfigInput = Partial<Omit<PgBouncerConfig, "auth" | "clientTls" | "serverTls">> & {
  databases: DatabaseTarget[];
  auth?: Partial<AuthConfig>;
  clientTls?: Partial<TlsSide>;
  serverTls?: Partial<TlsSide>;
};

export const DEFAULT_CONFIG: Omit<PgBouncerConfig, "databases"> = {
  listenAddr: "0.0.0.0",
  listenPort: 6432,
  poolMode: "transaction",
  maxClientConn: 500,
  defaultPoolSize: 20,
  minPoolSize: 0,
  reservePoolSize: 5,
  reservePoolTimeout: 3,
  maxDbConnections: 0,
  maxPreparedStatements: 200,
  auth: { type: "scram-sha-256", file: "/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt" },
  adminUsers: [],
  statsUsers: [],
  serverResetQuery: "DISCARD ALL",
  serverLifetime: 3600,
  serverIdleTimeout: 600,
  serverConnectTimeout: 15,
  queryWaitTimeout: 120,
  clientIdleTimeout: 0,
  idleTransactionTimeout: 0,
  ignoreStartupParameters: ["extra_float_digits"],
  logConnections: false,
  logPoolerErrors: true,
  clientTls: { mode: "disable" },
  serverTls: { mode: "prefer" },
  extra: {},
};

export const POOL_MODES: readonly PoolMode[] = ["session", "transaction", "statement"];
export const AUTH_TYPES: readonly AuthType[] = ["scram-sha-256", "md5", "plain", "cert", "hba"];
export const TLS_MODES: readonly TlsMode[] = ["disable", "allow", "prefer", "require", "verify-ca", "verify-full"];

/** Database names, user names and setting keys: no spaces, quotes, `=` or control characters. */
const NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.$-]{1,63}$/;
const KEY = /^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/;
/** Settings this kit writes itself; `extra` may not repeat them. */
const OWN_KEYS = new Set([
  "listen_addr", "listen_port", "pool_mode", "max_client_conn", "default_pool_size", "min_pool_size",
  "reserve_pool_size", "reserve_pool_timeout", "max_db_connections", "max_prepared_statements", "auth_type",
  "auth_file", "auth_query", "auth_user", "auth_dbname", "auth_hba_file", "admin_users", "stats_users", "server_reset_query",
  "server_lifetime", "server_idle_timeout", "server_connect_timeout", "query_wait_timeout", "client_idle_timeout",
  "idle_transaction_timeout", "ignore_startup_parameters", "log_connections", "log_disconnections",
  "log_pooler_errors",
]);

/** A value written into the ini file: one line, no control characters, no surrounding spaces. */
export function safeValue(v: string): boolean {
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
  return !/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(v) && v === v.trim();
}

/** Fills defaults and checks everything; throws `PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG` listing every problem. */
export function defineConfig(input: PgBouncerConfigInput): PgBouncerConfig {
  const config: PgBouncerConfig = {
    ...DEFAULT_CONFIG,
    ...input,
    databases: input.databases,
    auth: { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG.auth, ...input.auth },
    clientTls: { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG.clientTls, ...input.clientTls },
    serverTls: { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG.serverTls, ...input.serverTls },
    adminUsers: [...(input.adminUsers ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG.adminUsers)],
    statsUsers: [...(input.statsUsers ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG.statsUsers)],
    ignoreStartupParameters: [...(input.ignoreStartupParameters ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG.ignoreStartupParameters)],
    extra: { ...(input.extra ?? {}) },
  };
  const problems = checkConfig(config);
  if (problems.length) {
    throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG", `Invalid PgBouncer configuration:\n- ${problems.join("\n- ")}`, problems);
  }
  return config;
}

function checkConfig(c: PgBouncerConfig): string[] {
  const p: string[] = [];
  const int = (name: string, v: unknown, min: number, max = 1_000_000) => {
    if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isInteger(v) || v < min || v > max) p.push(`${name} must be a whole number from ${min} to ${max}`);
  };
  const str = (name: string, v: unknown) => {
    if (typeof v !== "string" || !v || !safeValue(v)) p.push(`${name} must be a non-empty single-line value`);
  };
  const name = (label: string, v: unknown) => {
    if (typeof v !== "string" || !NAME.test(v)) p.push(`${label} must be 1-63 letters, digits, _ . $ or -`);
  };

  str("listenAddr", c.listenAddr);
  if (typeof c.listenAddr === "string" && /[\s;]/.test(c.listenAddr.replace(/,\s*/g, ","))) p.push("listenAddr must be addresses separated by commas");
  int("listenPort", c.listenPort, 1, 65535);
  if (!POOL_MODES.includes(c.poolMode)) p.push(`poolMode must be one of ${POOL_MODES.join(", ")}`);
  int("maxClientConn", c.maxClientConn, 1);
  int("defaultPoolSize", c.defaultPoolSize, 1, 10_000);
  int("minPoolSize", c.minPoolSize, 0, 10_000);
  int("reservePoolSize", c.reservePoolSize, 0, 10_000);
  int("reservePoolTimeout", c.reservePoolTimeout, 0, 3600);
  int("maxDbConnections", c.maxDbConnections, 0, 100_000);
  int("maxPreparedStatements", c.maxPreparedStatements, 0, 100_000);
  int("serverLifetime", c.serverLifetime, 0, 604_800);
  int("serverIdleTimeout", c.serverIdleTimeout, 0, 604_800);
  int("serverConnectTimeout", c.serverConnectTimeout, 1, 3600);
  int("queryWaitTimeout", c.queryWaitTimeout, 0, 86_400);
  int("clientIdleTimeout", c.clientIdleTimeout, 0, 604_800);
  int("idleTransactionTimeout", c.idleTransactionTimeout, 0, 604_800);
  if (typeof c.minPoolSize === "number" && typeof c.defaultPoolSize === "number" && c.minPoolSize > c.defaultPoolSize) {
    p.push("minPoolSize cannot be larger than defaultPoolSize");
  }
  str("serverResetQuery", c.serverResetQuery);
  if (typeof c.logConnections !== "boolean") p.push("logConnections must be true or false");
  if (typeof c.logPoolerErrors !== "boolean") p.push("logPoolerErrors must be true or false");

  // auth
  const a = c.auth;
  if (!AUTH_TYPES.includes(a.type)) p.push(`auth.type must be one of ${AUTH_TYPES.join(", ")} (trust and any are not allowed)`);
  str("auth.file", a.file);
  if (a.query !== undefined) str("auth.query", a.query);
  if (a.user !== undefined) name("auth.user", a.user);
  if (a.dbname !== undefined) name("auth.dbname", a.dbname);
  if (a.query && !a.user && !c.databases.some((d) => d.authUser)) p.push("auth.query needs auth.user (or authUser on each database)");
  if (a.type === "hba") {
    if (!a.hbaFile) p.push("auth.type hba needs auth.hbaFile");
  }
  if (a.hbaFile !== undefined) str("auth.hbaFile", a.hbaFile);
  if (a.type === "cert" && c.clientTls.mode === "disable") p.push("auth.type cert needs clientTls");

  // users
  for (const [label, list] of [["adminUsers", c.adminUsers], ["statsUsers", c.statsUsers]] as const) {
    if (!Array.isArray(list)) p.push(`${label} must be a list`);
    else list.forEach((u, i) => name(`${label}[${i}]`, u));
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(c.ignoreStartupParameters)) p.push("ignoreStartupParameters must be a list");
  else c.ignoreStartupParameters.forEach((k, i) => {
    if (typeof k !== "string" || !KEY.test(k)) p.push(`ignoreStartupParameters[${i}] must be a parameter name`);
  });

  // databases
  if (!Array.isArray(c.databases) || c.databases.length === 0) p.push("databases needs at least one entry");
  else {
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    c.databases.forEach((d, i) => {
      const at = `databases[${i}]`;
      if (d.name !== "*") name(`${at}.name`, d.name);
      if (seen.has(d.name)) p.push(`${at}.name "${d.name}" is listed twice`);
      seen.add(d.name);
      if (d.name === "pgbouncer") p.push(`${at}.name "pgbouncer" is reserved for the admin console`);
      str(`${at}.host`, d.host);
      if (typeof d.host === "string" && /[\s'"\\=]/.test(d.host)) p.push(`${at}.host must not contain spaces, quotes, \\ or =`);
      if (d.port !== undefined) int(`${at}.port`, d.port, 1, 65535);
      if (d.dbname !== undefined) name(`${at}.dbname`, d.dbname);
      if (d.user !== undefined) name(`${at}.user`, d.user);
      if (d.authUser !== undefined) name(`${at}.authUser`, d.authUser);
      if (d.poolMode !== undefined && !POOL_MODES.includes(d.poolMode)) p.push(`${at}.poolMode must be one of ${POOL_MODES.join(", ")}`);
      if (d.poolSize !== undefined) int(`${at}.poolSize`, d.poolSize, 1, 10_000);
      if (d.minPoolSize !== undefined) int(`${at}.minPoolSize`, d.minPoolSize, 0, 10_000);
      if (d.reservePoolSize !== undefined) int(`${at}.reservePoolSize`, d.reservePoolSize, 0, 10_000);
      if (d.maxDbConnections !== undefined) int(`${at}.maxDbConnections`, d.maxDbConnections, 0, 100_000);
      if ("password" in (d as object)) p.push(`${at} must not carry a password (passwords belong in the userlist)`);
    });
  }

  // TLS
  for (const [side, t] of [["clientTls", c.clientTls], ["serverTls", c.serverTls]] as const) {
    if (!TLS_MODES.includes(t.mode)) p.push(`${side}.mode must be one of ${TLS_MODES.join(", ")}`);
    for (const k of ["certFile", "keyFile", "caFile", "protocols", "ciphers"] as const) if (t[k] !== undefined) str(`${side}.${k}`, t[k]);
    if ((t.certFile === undefined) !== (t.keyFile === undefined)) p.push(`${side}.certFile and ${side}.keyFile go together`);
  }
  if (c.clientTls.mode !== "disable" && (!c.clientTls.certFile || !c.clientTls.keyFile)) {
    p.push("clientTls needs certFile and keyFile unless its mode is disable");
  }
  for (const [side, t] of [["clientTls", c.clientTls], ["serverTls", c.serverTls]] as const) {
    if ((t.mode === "verify-ca" || t.mode === "verify-full") && !t.caFile) p.push(`${side}.mode ${t.mode} needs ${side}.caFile`);
  }

  // extra
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(c.extra ?? {})) {
    if (!KEY.test(k)) p.push(`extra key "${k}" is not a setting name`);
    else if (OWN_KEYS.has(k) || /^(client|server)_tls_/.test(k)) p.push(`extra.${k} is set by its own option; use that instead`);
    if (typeof v === "string" ? !safeValue(v) : typeof v !== "number" && typeof v !== "boolean") p.push(`extra.${k} must be a single-line string, a number or a boolean`);
  }
  return p;
}
```
