## File: src/env.ts

```ts
import {
  AUTH_TYPES,
  defineConfig,
  POOL_MODES,
  TLS_MODES,
  type AuthType,
  type DatabaseTarget,
  type PgBouncerConfig,
  type PgBouncerConfigInput,
  type PoolMode,
  type TlsMode,
  type TlsSide,
} from "./config";
import { PgBouncerError } from "./errors";
import { parsePostgresUrl } from "./url";
import type { SecretFormat, UserEntry } from "./userlist";

export type Env = Record<string, string | undefined>;

/** Every variable `configFromEnv` and `usersFromEnv` read, with what it sets. */
export const ENV_VARS: Record<string, string> = {
  PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL: "PostgreSQL URL PgBouncer forwards to (host, port, database; user and password go to the userlist)",
  PGBOUNCER_DATABASES: "More upstreams, comma-separated: [name=]postgres://… (name defaults to the URL's database)",
  PGBOUNCER_USERS: "Extra users, comma-separated user:secret (SCRAM verifier, md5 secret, or a percent-encoded password)",
  PGBOUNCER_USER_SECRET: "How plain passwords are stored: scram (default) | md5 | plain",
  PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_ADDR: "listen_addr (0.0.0.0)",
  PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_PORT: "listen_port (6432)",
  PGBOUNCER_POOL_MODE: "pool_mode: session | transaction (default) | statement",
  PGBOUNCER_MAX_CLIENT_CONN: "max_client_conn (500)",
  PGBOUNCER_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE: "default_pool_size (20)",
  PGBOUNCER_MIN_POOL_SIZE: "min_pool_size (0)",
  PGBOUNCER_RESERVE_POOL_SIZE: "reserve_pool_size (5)",
  PGBOUNCER_RESERVE_POOL_TIMEOUT: "reserve_pool_timeout in seconds (3)",
  PGBOUNCER_MAX_DB_CONNECTIONS: "max_db_connections (0 = no cap)",
  PGBOUNCER_MAX_PREPARED_STATEMENTS: "max_prepared_statements (200; 0 = off)",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_LIFETIME: "server_lifetime in seconds (3600)",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_IDLE_TIMEOUT: "server_idle_timeout in seconds (600)",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT: "server_connect_timeout in seconds (15)",
  PGBOUNCER_QUERY_WAIT_TIMEOUT: "query_wait_timeout in seconds (120)",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT: "client_idle_timeout in seconds (0 = off)",
  PGBOUNCER_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT: "idle_transaction_timeout in seconds (0 = off)",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_TYPE: "auth_type: scram-sha-256 (default) | md5 | plain | cert | hba",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_FILE: "auth_file (/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt)",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_QUERY: "auth_query (see AUTH_QUERY and authQuerySetupSql)",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_USER: "auth_user",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_PASSWORD: "Password of PGBOUNCER_AUTH_USER, written to the userlist in plain text (PgBouncer logs in as it)",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_DBNAME: "auth_dbname",
  PGBOUNCER_AUTH_HBA_FILE: "auth_hba_file (auth_type hba)",
  PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_USERS: "admin_users, comma-separated",
  PGBOUNCER_STATS_USERS: "stats_users, comma-separated",
  PGBOUNCER_IGNORE_STARTUP_PARAMETERS: "ignore_startup_parameters, comma-separated (extra_float_digits)",
  PGBOUNCER_LOG_CONNECTIONS: "log_connections and log_disconnections: true | false (false)",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_SSLMODE: "client_tls_sslmode, apps → PgBouncer (disable)",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_CERT_FILE: "client_tls_cert_file",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_KEY_FILE: "client_tls_key_file",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_CA_FILE: "client_tls_ca_file",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_PROTOCOLS: "client_tls_protocols",
  PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_TLS_CIPHERS: "client_tls_ciphers",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_SSLMODE: "server_tls_sslmode, PgBouncer → PostgreSQL (the upstream URL's sslmode, else prefer)",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_CERT_FILE: "server_tls_cert_file (client certificate for PostgreSQL)",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_KEY_FILE: "server_tls_key_file",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_CA_FILE: "server_tls_ca_file (the upstream URL's sslrootcert, if any)",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_PROTOCOLS: "server_tls_protocols",
  PGBOUNCER_SERVER_TLS_CIPHERS: "server_tls_ciphers",
};

interface Upstream {
  name: string;
  url: string;
}

function upstreams(env: Env, problems: string[]): Upstream[] {
  const out: Upstream[] = [];
  const add = (raw: string, from: string) => {
    const m = /^([A-Za-z0-9_.$-]+)=(postgres(?:ql)?:\/\/.*)$/.exec(raw);
    const url = m ? m[2]! : raw;
    try {
      const parsed = parsePostgresUrl(url);
      out.push({ name: m ? m[1]! : parsed.database, url });
    } catch (e) {
      problems.push(`${from}: ${(e as Error).message}`);
    }
  };
  if (env.PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL?.trim()) add(env.PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL.trim(), "PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL");
  for (const item of list(env.PGBOUNCER_DATABASES)) add(item, "PGBOUNCER_DATABASES");
  return out;
}

const list = (v: string | undefined) => (v ?? "").split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);

/**
 * Builds the configuration from environment variables (see `ENV_VARS`), on top of `base` and
 * the defaults. Throws `PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV` (bad variables) or `PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG`, listing every problem.
 */
export function configFromEnv(env: Env = process.env, base: Partial<PgBouncerConfigInput> = {}): PgBouncerConfig {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const get = (k: string) => {
    const v = env[k]?.trim();
    return v ? v : undefined;
  };
  const num = (k: string): number | undefined => {
    const v = get(k);
    if (v === undefined) return undefined;
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(v)) {
      problems.push(`${k} must be a whole number`);
      return undefined;
    }
    return Number(v);
  };
  const oneOf = <T extends string>(k: string, allowed: readonly T[]): T | undefined => {
    const v = get(k);
    if (v === undefined) return undefined;
    if (!allowed.includes(v as T)) {
      problems.push(`${k} must be one of ${allowed.join(", ")}`);
      return undefined;
    }
    return v as T;
  };
  const flag = (k: string): boolean | undefined => {
    const v = get(k)?.toLowerCase();
    if (v === undefined) return undefined;
    if (["1", "true", "yes", "on"].includes(v)) return true;
    if (["0", "false", "no", "off"].includes(v)) return false;
    problems.push(`${k} must be true or false`);
    return undefined;
  };

  const ups = upstreams(env, problems);
  const databases: DatabaseTarget[] = ups.map((u) => {
    const p = parsePostgresUrl(u.url);
    return { name: u.name, host: p.host, port: p.port, ...(p.database !== u.name ? { dbname: p.database } : {}) };
  });
  if (!env.PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL?.trim() && !list(env.PGBOUNCER_DATABASES).length && !base.databases?.length) problems.push("PGBOUNCER_UPSTREAM_URL (or PGBOUNCER_DATABASES) is required");

  // The first upstream's sslmode / sslrootcert describe PgBouncer → PostgreSQL.
  const first = ups[0] ? parsePostgresUrl(ups[0].url).params : {};
  const urlMode = first.sslmode as TlsMode | undefined;
  if (urlMode !== undefined && !TLS_MODES.includes(urlMode)) problems.push(`sslmode in the upstream URL must be one of ${TLS_MODES.join(", ")}`);

  const tls = (side: "CLIENT" | "SERVER", fallback: Partial<TlsSide>): Partial<TlsSide> => {
    const pre = `PGBOUNCER_${side}_TLS_`;
    const t: Partial<TlsSide> = { ...fallback };
    const mode = oneOf<TlsMode>(`${pre}SSLMODE`, TLS_MODES);
    if (mode) t.mode = mode;
    const files = { certFile: "CERT_FILE", keyFile: "KEY_FILE", caFile: "CA_FILE", protocols: "PROTOCOLS", ciphers: "CIPHERS" } as const;
    for (const [key, suffix] of Object.entries(files) as [keyof typeof files, string][]) {
      const v = get(pre + suffix);
      if (v !== undefined) t[key] = v;
    }
    return t;
  };

  const auth = {
    ...base.auth,
    ...defined({
      type: oneOf<AuthType>("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_TYPE", AUTH_TYPES),
      file: get("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_FILE"),
      query: get("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_QUERY"),
      user: get("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_USER"),
      dbname: get("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_DBNAME"),
      hbaFile: get("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_HBA_FILE"),
    }),
  };
  const input: PgBouncerConfigInput = {
    ...base,
    databases: databases.length ? databases : base.databases ?? [],
    ...defined({
      listenAddr: get("PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_ADDR"),
      listenPort: num("PGBOUNCER_LISTEN_PORT"),
      poolMode: oneOf<PoolMode>("PGBOUNCER_POOL_MODE", POOL_MODES),
      maxClientConn: num("PGBOUNCER_MAX_CLIENT_CONN"),
      defaultPoolSize: num("PGBOUNCER_DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE"),
      minPoolSize: num("PGBOUNCER_MIN_POOL_SIZE"),
      reservePoolSize: num("PGBOUNCER_RESERVE_POOL_SIZE"),
      reservePoolTimeout: num("PGBOUNCER_RESERVE_POOL_TIMEOUT"),
      maxDbConnections: num("PGBOUNCER_MAX_DB_CONNECTIONS"),
      maxPreparedStatements: num("PGBOUNCER_MAX_PREPARED_STATEMENTS"),
      serverLifetime: num("PGBOUNCER_SERVER_LIFETIME"),
      serverIdleTimeout: num("PGBOUNCER_SERVER_IDLE_TIMEOUT"),
      serverConnectTimeout: num("PGBOUNCER_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT"),
      queryWaitTimeout: num("PGBOUNCER_QUERY_WAIT_TIMEOUT"),
      clientIdleTimeout: num("PGBOUNCER_CLIENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT"),
      idleTransactionTimeout: num("PGBOUNCER_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT"),
      adminUsers: env.PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_USERS !== undefined ? list(env.PGBOUNCER_ADMIN_USERS) : undefined,
      statsUsers: env.PGBOUNCER_STATS_USERS !== undefined ? list(env.PGBOUNCER_STATS_USERS) : undefined,
      ignoreStartupParameters:
        env.PGBOUNCER_IGNORE_STARTUP_PARAMETERS !== undefined ? list(env.PGBOUNCER_IGNORE_STARTUP_PARAMETERS) : undefined,
      logConnections: flag("PGBOUNCER_LOG_CONNECTIONS"),
    }),
    auth,
    clientTls: tls("CLIENT", base.clientTls ?? {}),
    serverTls: tls("SERVER", {
      ...base.serverTls,
      ...defined({ mode: TLS_MODES.includes(urlMode as TlsMode) ? urlMode : undefined, caFile: first.sslrootcert }),
    }),
  };
  if (problems.length) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV", `Invalid PgBouncer environment:\n- ${problems.join("\n- ")}`, problems);
  return defineConfig(input);
}

/**
 * The userlist entries from the environment: the user and password of every upstream URL, then
 * `PGBOUNCER_USERS`. Pass them to `renderUserlist(entries, secretFormatFromEnv(env))`.
 */
export function usersFromEnv(env: Env = process.env): UserEntry[] {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const byUser = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const u of upstreams(env, problems)) {
    const p = parsePostgresUrl(u.url);
    if (p.user && p.password && !byUser.has(p.user)) byUser.set(p.user, p.password);
  }
  for (const item of list(env.PGBOUNCER_USERS)) {
    const i = item.indexOf(":");
    if (i <= 0 || i === item.length - 1) {
      problems.push("PGBOUNCER_USERS entries are user:secret");
      continue;
    }
    const user = item.slice(0, i);
    let secret = item.slice(i + 1);
    if (!secret.startsWith("SCRAM-SHA-256$") && !/^md5[0-9a-f]{32}$/.test(secret)) {
      try {
        secret = decodeURIComponent(secret);
      } catch {
        problems.push(`PGBOUNCER_USERS: the password of ${user} is not valid percent-encoding`);
        continue;
      }
    }
    byUser.set(user, secret);
  }
  const authUser = env.PGBOUNCER_AUTH_USER?.trim();
  const authPassword = env.PGBOUNCER_AUTH_PASSWORD;
  if (authPassword && !authUser) problems.push("PGBOUNCER_AUTH_PASSWORD needs PGBOUNCER_AUTH_USER");
  if (problems.length) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV", `Invalid PgBouncer environment:\n- ${problems.join("\n- ")}`, problems);
  const entries: UserEntry[] = [...byUser].filter(([user]) => !(authPassword && user === authUser)).map(([user, secret]) => ({ user, secret }));
  if (authUser && authPassword) entries.push({ user: authUser, secret: authPassword, format: "plain" });
  return entries;
}

/** `PGBOUNCER_USER_SECRET`: scram (default), md5 or plain. */
export function secretFormatFromEnv(env: Env = process.env): SecretFormat {
  const v = env.PGBOUNCER_USER_SECRET?.trim() || "scram";
  if (v !== "scram" && v !== "md5" && v !== "plain") {
    throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV", "PGBOUNCER_USER_SECRET must be one of scram, md5, plain", ["PGBOUNCER_USER_SECRET must be one of scram, md5, plain"]);
  }
  return v;
}

function defined<T extends object>(o: T): { [K in keyof T]?: Exclude<T[K], undefined> } {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(o).filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined)) as { [K in keyof T]?: Exclude<T[K], undefined> };
}
```

## File: src/errors.ts

```ts
/** Error codes are a public contract: add, never rename. */
export type PgBouncerErrorCode =
  | "PGBOUNCER_BAD_CONFIG"
  | "PGBOUNCER_BAD_ENV"
  | "PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL"
  | "PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER"
  | "PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE";

export class PgBouncerError extends Error {
  readonly code: PgBouncerErrorCode;
  /** Every problem found, when there was more than one (configuration and environment checks). */
  readonly problems: string[];

  constructor(code: PgBouncerErrorCode, message: string, problems: string[] = [message]) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "PgBouncerError";
    this.code = code;
    this.problems = problems;
  }
}

export const isPgBouncerError = (e: unknown): e is PgBouncerError => e instanceof PgBouncerError;
```

## File: src/health.ts

```ts
import { connect } from "node:net";
import { PgBouncerError } from "./errors";

export interface ProbeOptions {
  /** Default `127.0.0.1`. */
  host?: string;
  /** Default 6432. */
  port?: number;
  /** Default 2000 ms. */
  timeoutMs?: number;
}

export interface ProbeResult {
  ok: boolean;
  /** The server accepted TLS (`S`) or declined it (`N`); `null` when the probe failed. */
  tls: boolean | null;
  latencyMs: number;
  /** Why it failed (no credentials, host names or addresses beyond what you passed). */
  error?: string;
}

/** The PostgreSQL SSLRequest packet: length 8, code 80877103. */
const SSL_REQUEST = Buffer.from([0, 0, 0, 8, 0x04, 0xd2, 0x16, 0x2f]);

/**
 * Is PgBouncer (or PostgreSQL) up and speaking the protocol? Opens a TCP connection, sends an
 * SSLRequest and reads the one-byte answer, then closes. No credentials, no query, no pool slot used.
 */
export function probePgBouncer(opts: ProbeOptions = {}): Promise<ProbeResult> {
  const host = opts.host ?? "127.0.0.1";
  const port = opts.port ?? 6432;
  const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? 2000;
  const started = performance.now();
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let done = false;
    const socket = connect({ host, port });
    const finish = (r: Omit<ProbeResult, "latencyMs">) => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      socket.destroy();
      resolve({ ...r, latencyMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started) });
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => finish({ ok: false, tls: null, error: `no answer within ${timeoutMs} ms` }), timeoutMs);
    socket.once("connect", () => socket.write(SSL_REQUEST));
    socket.once("data", (b) => {
      const c = String.fromCharCode(b[0] ?? 0);
      if (c === "S" || c === "N") finish({ ok: true, tls: c === "S" });
      else finish({ ok: false, tls: null, error: "not a PostgreSQL protocol answer" });
    });
    socket.once("error", (e: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => finish({ ok: false, tls: null, error: e.code ?? "connection failed" }));
    socket.once("close", () => finish({ ok: false, tls: null, error: "connection closed" }));
  });
}

export interface WaitOptions extends ProbeOptions {
  /** Total time to wait. Default 30 000 ms. */
  waitMs?: number;
  /** Pause between probes. Default 500 ms. */
  intervalMs?: number;
}

/** Probes until PgBouncer answers; throws `PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE` after `waitMs`. For start-up scripts. */
export async function waitForPgBouncer(opts: WaitOptions = {}): Promise<ProbeResult> {
  const end = Date.now() + (opts.waitMs ?? 30_000);
  let last: ProbeResult;
  for (;;) {
    last = await probePgBouncer(opts);
    if (last.ok) return last;
    if (Date.now() >= end) break;
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, opts.intervalMs ?? 500));
  }
  throw new PgBouncerError(
    "PGBOUNCER_UNREACHABLE",
    `PgBouncer at ${opts.host ?? "127.0.0.1"}:${opts.port ?? 6432} did not answer (${last.error ?? "unknown"})`,
  );
}

export interface ReadinessOptions extends ProbeOptions {
  /**
   * Optional end-to-end check through the pool, with your own driver, e.g.
   * `() => sequelize.query("SELECT 1")`. Without it only the protocol probe runs.
   */
  query?: () => Promise<unknown>;
  /** Default 3000 ms for the query. */
  queryTimeoutMs?: number;
}

export interface Readiness {
  ok: boolean;
  pgbouncer: ProbeResult;
  query?: { ok: boolean; latencyMs: number; error?: string };
}

/**
 * A readiness check for a health endpoint (`GET /health`, a Kubernetes readiness probe, compose
 * `depends_on`). Framework-agnostic: call it and send the result. Errors are summarised, never thrown.
 */
export function readiness(opts: ReadinessOptions = {}): () => Promise<Readiness> {
  return async () => {
    const pgbouncer = await probePgBouncer(opts);
    if (!pgbouncer.ok || !opts.query) return { ok: pgbouncer.ok, pgbouncer };
    const started = performance.now();
    const limit = opts.queryTimeoutMs ?? 3000;
    let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
    try {
      await Promise.race([
        opts.query(),
        new Promise((_, reject) => (timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`query took longer than ${limit} ms`)), limit))),
      ]);
      return { ok: true, pgbouncer, query: { ok: true, latencyMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started) } };
    } catch (e) {
      // the driver's message only: it may name a database but never a password
      const error = e instanceof Error ? e.message.split("\n")[0]!.slice(0, 200) : "query failed";
      return { ok: false, pgbouncer, query: { ok: false, latencyMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started), error } };
    } finally {
      clearTimeout(timer);
    }
  };
}
```

## File: src/ini.ts

```ts
import { defineConfig, type DatabaseTarget, type PgBouncerConfig, type PgBouncerConfigInput, type TlsSide } from "./config";

const bool = (v: boolean) => (v ? "1" : "0");
/** libpq-style value for a [databases] connection string. */
const connValue = (v: string | number) => {
  const s = String(v);
  return /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$/.test(s) ? s : `'${s.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\").replace(/'/g, "\\'")}'`;
};

function databaseLine(d: DatabaseTarget): string {
  const parts: [string, string | number | undefined][] = [
    ["host", d.host],
    ["port", d.port ?? 5432],
    ["dbname", d.dbname ?? (d.name === "*" ? undefined : d.name)],
    ["user", d.user],
    ["auth_user", d.authUser],
    ["pool_mode", d.poolMode],
    ["pool_size", d.poolSize],
    ["min_pool_size", d.minPoolSize],
    ["reserve_pool", d.reservePoolSize],
    ["max_db_connections", d.maxDbConnections],
  ];
  return `${d.name} = ${parts.filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined).map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${connValue(v!)}`).join(" ")}`;
}

function tlsLines(prefix: "client" | "server", t: TlsSide): string[] {
  const out = [`${prefix}_tls_sslmode = ${t.mode}`];
  if (t.certFile) out.push(`${prefix}_tls_cert_file = ${t.certFile}`);
  if (t.keyFile) out.push(`${prefix}_tls_key_file = ${t.keyFile}`);
  if (t.caFile) out.push(`${prefix}_tls_ca_file = ${t.caFile}`);
  if (t.protocols) out.push(`${prefix}_tls_protocols = ${t.protocols}`);
  if (t.ciphers) out.push(`${prefix}_tls_ciphers = ${t.ciphers}`);
  return out;
}

/**
 * Renders pgbouncer.ini. Takes a full config or the input to `defineConfig` (checked either way).
 * The file holds no passwords; they live in the userlist (`renderUserlist`).
 */
export function renderIni(config: PgBouncerConfig | PgBouncerConfigInput): string {
  const c = defineConfig(config);
  const a = c.auth;
  const lines = [
    "; Generated by @mgpl-diagnostics/pgbouncer-kit. Edit the configuration, not this file.",
    "",
    "[databases]",
    ...c.databases.map(databaseLine),
    "",
    "[pgbouncer]",
    `listen_addr = ${c.listenAddr}`,
    `listen_port = ${c.listenPort}`,
    "",
    `auth_type = ${a.type}`,
    `auth_file = ${a.file}`,
    ...(a.query ? [`auth_query = ${a.query}`] : []),
    ...(a.user ? [`auth_user = ${a.user}`] : []),
    ...(a.dbname ? [`auth_dbname = ${a.dbname}`] : []),
    ...(a.hbaFile ? [`auth_hba_file = ${a.hbaFile}`] : []),
    ...(c.adminUsers.length ? [`admin_users = ${c.adminUsers.join(", ")}`] : []),
    ...(c.statsUsers.length ? [`stats_users = ${c.statsUsers.join(", ")}`] : []),
    "",
    `pool_mode = ${c.poolMode}`,
    `max_client_conn = ${c.maxClientConn}`,
    `default_pool_size = ${c.defaultPoolSize}`,
    `min_pool_size = ${c.minPoolSize}`,
    `reserve_pool_size = ${c.reservePoolSize}`,
    `reserve_pool_timeout = ${c.reservePoolTimeout}`,
    `max_db_connections = ${c.maxDbConnections}`,
    `max_prepared_statements = ${c.maxPreparedStatements}`,
    "",
    `server_reset_query = ${c.serverResetQuery}`,
    `server_lifetime = ${c.serverLifetime}`,
    `server_idle_timeout = ${c.serverIdleTimeout}`,
    `server_connect_timeout = ${c.serverConnectTimeout}`,
    `query_wait_timeout = ${c.queryWaitTimeout}`,
    `client_idle_timeout = ${c.clientIdleTimeout}`,
    `idle_transaction_timeout = ${c.idleTransactionTimeout}`,
    ...(c.ignoreStartupParameters.length ? [`ignore_startup_parameters = ${c.ignoreStartupParameters.join(",")}`] : []),
    "",
    ...tlsLines("client", c.clientTls),
    ...tlsLines("server", c.serverTls),
    "",
    `log_connections = ${bool(c.logConnections)}`,
    `log_disconnections = ${bool(c.logConnections)}`,
    `log_pooler_errors = ${bool(c.logPoolerErrors)}`,
  ];
  const extra = Object.entries(c.extra);
  if (extra.length) lines.push("", ...extra.map(([k, v]) => `${k} = ${typeof v === "boolean" ? bool(v) : v}`));
  return `${lines.join("\n")}\n`;
}
```

## File: src/url.ts

```ts
import { PgBouncerError } from "./errors";

/** A PostgreSQL connection URL, decoded. */
export interface PostgresUrl {
  host: string;
  port: number;
  database: string;
  user?: string;
  password?: string;
  /** Query parameters (`sslmode`, `application_name`, …), decoded. */
  params: Record<string, string>;
}

const SCHEMES = new Set(["postgres:", "postgresql:"]);

/** Parses `postgres://user:password@host:port/database?params`. Throws `PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL`. */
export function parsePostgresUrl(url: string): PostgresUrl {
  let u: URL;
  try {
    u = new URL(url);
  } catch {
    throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL", "Not a valid PostgreSQL URL");
  }
  if (!SCHEMES.has(u.protocol)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL", "A PostgreSQL URL starts with postgres:// or postgresql://");
  const host = u.hostname.replace(/^\[(.*)\]$/, "$1");
  if (!host) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_URL", "The PostgreSQL URL has no host");
  const port = u.port ? Number(u.port) : 5432;
  const database = decodeURIComponent(u.pathname.replace(/^\//, ""));
  const params: Record<string, string> = {};
  u.searchParams.forEach((v, k) => (params[k] = v));
  return {
    host,
    port,
    database: database || (u.username ? decodeURIComponent(u.username) : "postgres"),
    ...(u.username ? { user: decodeURIComponent(u.username) } : {}),
    ...(u.password ? { password: decodeURIComponent(u.password) } : {}),
    params,
  };
}

export interface PgBouncerUrlOptions {
  /** PgBouncer's host as the app sees it (compose service name, `127.0.0.1`, …). */
  host: string;
  /** Default 6432. */
  port?: number;
  /** The database name in PgBouncer's [databases] section, when it differs from the upstream one. */
  database?: string;
}

/**
 * The app's DATABASE_URL rewritten to go through PgBouncer: same user, password and parameters,
 * PgBouncer's host and port. `sslmode` is kept, because it now describes app → PgBouncer.
 */
export function pgbouncerUrl(databaseUrl: string, opts: PgBouncerUrlOptions): string {
  const parsed = parsePostgresUrl(databaseUrl);
  const u = new URL(databaseUrl);
  u.hostname = opts.host.includes(":") && !opts.host.startsWith("[") ? `[${opts.host}]` : opts.host;
  u.port = String(opts.port ?? 6432);
  u.pathname = `/${encodeURIComponent(opts.database ?? parsed.database)}`;
  return u.toString();
}
```

## File: src/userlist.ts

```ts
import { createHash, createHmac, pbkdf2Sync, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import { PgBouncerError } from "./errors";

/** PostgreSQL's default `scram_iterations`. */
export const SCRAM_ITERATIONS = 4096;

const USER = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.$-]{1,63}$/;
const SCRAM = /^SCRAM-SHA-256\$(\d+):([A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*)\$([A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*):([A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*)$/;
const MD5 = /^md5[0-9a-f]{32}$/;

function checkUser(user: string): void {
  if (typeof user !== "string" || !USER.test(user)) {
    throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", "A user name must be 1-63 letters, digits, _ . $ or -");
  }
}

// ---- SASLprep (RFC 4013), as PostgreSQL applies it before hashing ------------------------------

const NON_ASCII_SPACE = /[   -​  　]/g;
const MAPPED_TO_NOTHING = /[­͏᠆᠋-᠍‌‍⁠︀-️﻿]/g;
// eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
const PROHIBITED = /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f̀́‎‏‪-‮⁪-⁯-￹-�]|[\ud800-\udfff]/;

/**
 * PostgreSQL normalises a SCRAM password with SASLprep and, when the password is not valid
 * SASLprep input, hashes the raw UTF-8 bytes instead. This does the same.
 */
export function saslprep(password: string): string {
  if (/^[\x20-\x7e]*$/.test(password)) return password;
  const mapped = password.replace(NON_ASCII_SPACE, " ").replace(MAPPED_TO_NOTHING, "").normalize("NFKC");
  if (!mapped || PROHIBITED.test(mapped)) return password;
  return mapped;
}

export interface ScramOptions {
  /** 16 random bytes by default. Pass the server's salt to reproduce its verifier. */
  salt?: Uint8Array;
  /** Default 4096 (PostgreSQL's default). */
  iterations?: number;
}

/**
 * A SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier in PostgreSQL's format (`SCRAM-SHA-256$<iter>:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>`).
 * It is what `pg_authid.rolpassword` holds, and what PgBouncer's userlist takes.
 */
export function scramVerifier(password: string, opts: ScramOptions = {}): string {
  if (typeof password !== "string" || !password) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", "The password is empty");
  const iterations = opts.iterations ?? SCRAM_ITERATIONS;
  if (!Number.isInteger(iterations) || iterations < 1) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", "iterations must be a positive whole number");
  const salt = Buffer.from(opts.salt ?? randomBytes(16));
  const salted = pbkdf2Sync(Buffer.from(saslprep(password), "utf8"), salt, iterations, 32, "sha256");
  const clientKey = createHmac("sha256", salted).update("Client Key").digest();
  const storedKey = createHash("sha256").update(clientKey).digest();
  const serverKey = createHmac("sha256", salted).update("Server Key").digest();
  return `SCRAM-SHA-256$${iterations}:${salt.toString("base64")}$${storedKey.toString("base64")}:${serverKey.toString("base64")}`;
}

/** Splits a verifier into its parts; `null` when it is not one. */
export function parseScramVerifier(v: string): { iterations: number; salt: Buffer; storedKey: Buffer; serverKey: Buffer } | null {
  const m = SCRAM.exec(v);
  if (!m) return null;
  return { iterations: Number(m[1]), salt: Buffer.from(m[2]!, "base64"), storedKey: Buffer.from(m[3]!, "base64"), serverKey: Buffer.from(m[4]!, "base64") };
}

/** Does `password` match this SCRAM verifier? (Useful to check a userlist against a known password.) */
export function verifyScram(password: string, verifier: string): boolean {
  const p = parseScramVerifier(verifier);
  if (!p) return false;
  return scramVerifier(password, { salt: p.salt, iterations: p.iterations }) === verifier;
}

/** PostgreSQL's legacy MD5 secret: `"md5" + md5(password + user)`. Prefer SCRAM. */
export function md5Secret(user: string, password: string): string {
  checkUser(user);
  if (typeof password !== "string" || !password) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", "The password is empty");
  return `md5${createHash("md5").update(password + user).digest("hex")}`;
}

export const isScramVerifier = (s: string): boolean => SCRAM.test(s);
export const isMd5Secret = (s: string): boolean => MD5.test(s);

/** How a plain password is written to the userlist. */
export type SecretFormat = "scram" | "md5" | "plain";

export interface UserEntry {
  user: string;
  /**
   * A SCRAM verifier or MD5 secret (written as it is), or a plain password, which is converted with
   * `format` (`scram` by default).
   */
  secret: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the list's format for this entry. The `auth_user` of `auth_query` needs `plain`:
   * PgBouncer logs in as that user itself, so a SCRAM verifier cannot be passed through for it.
   */
  format?: SecretFormat;
}

/** Turns one entry's secret into what the userlist stores. */
export function userSecret(entry: UserEntry, format: SecretFormat = "scram", opts: ScramOptions = {}): string {
  checkUser(entry.user);
  format = entry.format ?? format;
  const s = entry.secret;
  if (typeof s !== "string" || !s) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", `User ${entry.user} has no password`);
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
  if (/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(s)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", `The password of ${entry.user} contains a control character`);
  if (isScramVerifier(s) || isMd5Secret(s)) return s;
  if (s.startsWith("SCRAM-SHA-256$")) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", `The SCRAM verifier of ${entry.user} is malformed`);
  if (format === "scram") return scramVerifier(s, opts);
  if (format === "md5") return md5Secret(entry.user, s);
  return s;
}

const quote = (s: string) => `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;

/**
 * Renders userlist.txt (`"user" "secret"` per line). Plain passwords are converted to `format`
 * (SCRAM by default), so the file holds no password unless you ask for `plain`.
 */
export function renderUserlist(entries: UserEntry[], format: SecretFormat = "scram", opts: ScramOptions = {}): string {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const lines = entries.map((e) => {
    checkUser(e.user);
    if (seen.has(e.user)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", `User ${e.user} is listed twice`);
    seen.add(e.user);
    return `${quote(e.user)} ${quote(userSecret(e, format, opts))}`;
  });
  return lines.length ? `${lines.join("\n")}\n` : "";
}

/** Reads a userlist back into entries (comments with `;` or `#`, blank lines ignored). */
export function parseUserlist(text: string): UserEntry[] {
  const out: UserEntry[] = [];
  const field = /"((?:[^"]|"")*)"/y;
  for (const raw of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const line = raw.trim();
    if (!line || line.startsWith(";") || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
    field.lastIndex = 0;
    const u = field.exec(line);
    const rest = line.slice(field.lastIndex).trimStart();
    field.lastIndex = 0;
    const p = field.exec(rest);
    if (!u || !p) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", "Malformed userlist line");
    out.push({ user: u[1]!.replace(/""/g, '"'), secret: p[1]!.replace(/""/g, '"') });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The query that reads the verifiers PostgreSQL already holds (run as a superuser). Feed the rows
 * to `userlistFromRows`: the userlist then matches the server exactly, which SCRAM pass-through needs.
 */
export const PG_SHADOW_QUERY = "SELECT usename, passwd FROM pg_catalog.pg_shadow WHERE passwd IS NOT NULL AND NOT usesuper";

export function userlistFromRows(rows: { usename: string; passwd: string | null }[]): string {
  return renderUserlist(rows.filter((r) => r.passwd).map((r) => ({ user: r.usename, secret: r.passwd! })), "plain");
}

/**
 * SQL that sets a role's password to this exact verifier, so PostgreSQL and PgBouncer hold the same
 * SCRAM secret. PostgreSQL stores a pre-hashed verifier as it is; the password itself never reaches the server.
 */
export function alterRoleSql(user: string, verifier: string): string {
  checkUser(user);
  if (!isScramVerifier(verifier)) throw new PgBouncerError("PGBOUNCER_BAD_USER", "alterRoleSql takes a SCRAM verifier, not a password");
  return `ALTER ROLE ${quote(user)} PASSWORD '${verifier}';`;
}

/** The function `authQuerySetupSql` creates, and the `auth.query` that calls it. */
export const AUTH_QUERY = "SELECT uname, phash FROM pgbouncer.user_lookup($1)";

/**
 * SQL (run once as a superuser, in the database `auth.dbname` names) for PgBouncer's `auth_query`:
 * a login role for PgBouncer, and a SECURITY DEFINER lookup that never returns superusers.
 * Give that role a password and put it in the userlist with `format: "plain"` (PgBouncer logs in as
 * it, so it needs the password itself; keep the userlist file at mode 600).
 */
export function authQuerySetupSql(authUser = "pgbouncer_auth"): string {
  checkUser(authUser);
  const role = quote(authUser);
  return `DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = '${authUser}') THEN
    CREATE ROLE ${role} LOGIN;
  END IF;
END $$;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS pgbouncer;
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA pgbouncer FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA pgbouncer TO ${role};
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION pgbouncer.user_lookup(i_username text, OUT uname text, OUT phash text)
RETURNS record LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp AS $fn$
BEGIN
  SELECT usename, passwd INTO uname, phash FROM pg_catalog.pg_shadow
  WHERE usename = i_username AND NOT usesuper;
  RETURN;
END
$fn$;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION pgbouncer.user_lookup(text) FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pgbouncer.user_lookup(text) TO ${role};
`;
}
```
